item.content:encoded:
Bryce Harper Reacts to Game-Tying HR After Misplay in Phillies Win vs. Braves in MLB Playoffs G2
Philadelphia Phillies star Bryce Harper had quite the sequence between the bottom of the seventh inning and the top of the eighth during his team's 4-3 win Wednesday
A costly fielding error ultimately led to a pair of Braves' runs, allowing them to take a 3-1 lead. But Harper then followed up Kyle Schwarber's solo homer with one of his own the very next inning, tying the game right back up.
Harper spoke about both moments following the win:
"You've got to flush [the mistake] as quickly as possible knowing that [Braves' pitcher Dylan Lee] is coming into the game," Harper said. "And obviously I was hearing it pretty good from Braves' and Phillies' fans behind the dugout. So gotta show up in that situation. Kyle had a great at-bat and then... I wasn't not trying to hit a homer, I'll tell you that."
Harper primarily played first base this season and shifted to right field after second baseman Luis Arráez—who is unavailable for this series due to a sprained ankle suffered last Thursday—was acquired at the trade deadline, requiring a reshuffling of the infield. He's generally been steady since moving back to the outfield, though Wednesday's error was nearly costly.
And his redemption arc wasn't complete without a few of his teammates chipping in.
There was pitcher Andrew Painter, who came out of the bullpen and threw three scoreless innings, earning the win. Not too shabby for Philadelphia's fifth starter, who isn't accustomed to pitching out of the bullpen.
Or as Harper described Painter's performance: "Absolute dawg mentality, closes the door for us."
And then there was Alec Bohm, who put the Phillies up by a run in the top of the 10th inning with an opposite-field homer.
"No, I didn't," Bohm admitted in his post-game interview on NBC when asked if he knew he hit a homer off the bat. "I don't really know what happened. I was trying to pull the ball off the foul pole and I hit it to right field so, I'll take it."

김하성은 1일(한국시간) 미국 조지아주 애틀랜타 트루이스트파크에서 열린 내셔널리그(NL) 와일드카드 시리즈(WC·3전 2승제) 2차전 필라델피아 필리스와 경기에서 1타수 무안타 1볼넷 1득점을 기록했습니다.
9번 타자 유격수로 선발 출전한 김하성은 3회말 선두타자로 볼넷을 골라 출루했고, 5회에는 포수 파울플라이로 잡혔습니다.
1대 1인 7회말 노아웃 1루에서는 희생번트를 댔으나, 야수선택으로 처리하면서 살아 나간 뒤 맷 올슨의 희생플라이 때 득점까지 기록했습니다.

item.title: [roundtable.io] Pirates' Paul Skenes Has Clear Feelings About Potential Salary Cap
item.dc:creator: Jon Conahan
item.description: Skenes knows better. Right now, it's hard to say what will happen in Major League Baseball with the expected lockout. item.content:encoded:
Skenes knows better.
Right now, it's hard to say what will happen in Major League Baseball with the expected lockout. Plenty still needs to be figured out, though teams across the league will ultimately make those decisions by bargaining with some of the sport's top players.
There's plenty of reason to believe Skenes will do what's needed to ensure guys get paid as they have in the past, since that would benefit him. Skenes is undoubtedly one of the best players in Major League Baseball, and when his free agency comes, there's a strong argument that he'll be the highest-paid pitcher in MLB history.
However, many are forgetting there are other factors at play in this potential lockout, including players who aren't going to be paid like some of the biggest stars in Major League Baseball history.
Whether it's arbitration hearings, contract extensions, or anything in between, there's a lot to answer over the next couple of months, and it doesn't seem like baseball has a clear answer.
For Pittsburgh specifically, the Pirates have a lot to figure out, as they're a team that typically doesn't want to pay guys, and some of this could benefit them.
“When Skenes was asked what the biggest point of negotiations would be, he said he believes it is more than one, but he understands it all centers around a salary cap.
“He presented it from a Pirates perspective: The Pirates are a young team, where most players have not yet reached arbitration. Those players’ primary focus will be raising the minimum salary. The players who have hit arbitration will want those figures to increase. The few who have long-term contracts will want to ensure those contracts remain guaranteed,” Colin Beazley wrote.
As Skenes touched on here, the Pirates' young team is a bit polarizing when it comes to the expected lockout.
The Pirates as an organization would likely benefit from not paying some of these guys as much as they're worth, if that's what the salary cap ends up doing, if baseball goes that way, but Pittsburgh might be able to field a better team because of it and even keep a guy like Skenes around eventually.
I'm curious to see how all of that goes, like everybody else, but sneakily, the Pirates are undoubtedly one of the more interesting teams in the league to follow because of this.

item.title: [Sportsnet.ca] White Sox chase Astros ace Hunter Brown in first inning of Game 2
item.dc:creator: Sportsnet Staff
item.description: After dropping Game 1 of their wild-card series to the Chicago White Sox while throwing a bullpen day, the Houston Astros had to feel a sense of relief knowing they were turning to their ace, Hunter Brown, for Game 2. But as the second inning came around on Wednesday, Brown had already been chased from the contest. item.content:encoded:
After dropping Game 1 of their wild-card series to the Chicago White Sox while throwing a bullpen day, the Houston Astros had to feel a sense of relief knowing they were turning to their ace, Hunter Brown, for Game 2.
But as the second inning came around on Wednesday, Brown had already been chased from the contest.
Chicago sent 10 batters to the plate in a four-run first, tagging Brown for five hits as it looked to win its first playoff series since 2005.
Brown managed to get two outs — both by way of the strikeout — before manager Joe Espada made the move to the bullpen.
White Sox leadoff hitter Sam Antonacci wasted little time putting Brown on his back foot, opening the game with a double that went off Astros left fielder Yordan Alvarez's glove. Kyle Teel then brought home Antonacci with a single, Miguel Vargas reached on an error, Andrew Benintendi scored both with a single and Tristan Peters completed the rally with an RBI single of his own.
Brown left with the bases loaded and two out, but Tuesday's opener, AJ Blubaugh, entered and escaped the jam.
Houston's pitching staff has been ravaged by injuries this season, leaving the 28-year-old Brown and Hayden Wesneski as their lone healthy starters for the playoffs.
With the Astros not clinching their AL West title until the final day of the regular season, they weren't able to line up their pitching staff, which led to the bullpen day in Game 1 before Brown and Wesneski could return on normal rest.
"Having those guys healthy with regular rest, it's super valuable for us," Espdada said before the series began, making Brown's short start all the more costly for an Astros team already needing length from their pitchers.
Brown finished the 2026 regular season with a 3.19 ERA and 124 strikeouts over 107.1 innings. He was also hit by the injury bug earlier in the season, which limited the six-foot-two right-hander to just 20 starts.

item.content:encoded:
Jonathan Aranda se prepara para afrontar una nueva etapa en una temporada que ha representado un gran salto en su carrera. El pelotero tijuanense buscará mantener su nivel con los Tampa Bay Rays durante los Playoffs de la MLB 2026, después de una campaña regular en la que el equipo aseguró el campeonato de la División Este de la Liga Americana.
La novena de Tampa Bay llega a la postemporada con el objetivo de avanzar en la pelea por el título. Aranda tendrá un papel importante en el lineup de los Rays, donde su producción ofensiva y regularidad serán elementos a seguir durante cada encuentro. El mexicano buscará trasladar el buen momento de la fase regular a los duelos de mayor presión del calendario.
La afición mexicana podrá seguir de cerca la actuación del jugador nacido en Tijuana a través de las opciones oficiales de transmisión. Las plataformas de televisión y servicios digitales permitirán disfrutar cada turno al bate, jugada defensiva y momento clave de Aranda en una postemporada que representa una nueva oportunidad para destacar en las Grandes Ligas. Aquí en Heraldo Deportes te platicamos todos los detalles.
Este es el CALENDARIO de juegos de Jonathan Aranda y Rays en Playoffs 2026
Los Tampa Bay Rays iniciarán su camino en los Playoffs de la MLB 2026 con la mira puesta en avanzar en la postemporada y aprovechar su condición de locales en los primeros encuentros. El equipo de Tampa Bay tendrá una serie exigente desde el comienzo, con varios partidos definidos y otros horarios que todavía están pendientes de confirmación:
- Juego 1: sábado 3 de octubre, 16:30 horas - Tropicana Field.
- Juego 2: lunes 5 de octubre, 18:00 horas- Tropicana Field.
- Juego 3: miércoles 7 de octubre, horario por definir -Nueva York o Boston.
- Juego 4*: jueves 8 de octubre, horario por definir- Nueva York o Boston.
- Juego 5*: sábado 10 de octubre, horario por definir - Tropicana Field.
Los encuentros marcados con asterisco solo se disputarían si la serie llega a esas instancias. Para la afición mexicana, los primeros dos compromisos ya cuentan con horario establecido, mientras que las fechas restantes dependerán del desarrollo de la serie y de la programación oficial de las Grandes Ligas.
Te puede interesar: ¡Ben Rice desapareció la pelota! Así fue su tremendo jonrón con Yankees ante Red Sox en la MLB | VIDEO
¿Dónde ver EN VIVO los juegos de Jonathan Aranda y Rays en Playoffs 2026?
La afición mexicana tendrá diferentes alternativas para seguir los partidos de los Playoffs de la MLB 2026. Los encuentros de la Liga Americana estarán disponibles a través de ESPN en televisión de paga, una opción para quienes buscan disfrutar en vivo cada aparición de Jonathan Aranda con los Tampa Bay Rays.
También será posible seguir la postemporada mediante opciones de streaming. Los aficionados podrán recurrir a Disney+ para ver los encuentros disponibles en la plataforma o contratar el paquete correspondiente de los Playoffs a través de MLB.TV, ampliando las alternativas para acompañar al pelotero tijuanense durante su participación en la fase decisiva.
¿Quién será el rival de Jonathan Aranda y Rays en estos Playoffs 2026?
Jonathan Aranda y los Tampa Bay Rays ya conocen el camino que deberán seguir en la postemporada, aunque todavía esperan la definición de su próximo rival. El equipo de Tampa Bay se enfrentará al ganador de la Serie de Comodines entre los New York Yankees y los Boston Red Sox, en un duelo que determinará quién avanzará para medirse ante los Rays.

item.content:encoded:
Pat Murphy provided an update on Joey Ortiz as the Milwaukee Brewers prepare for their National League Division Series opener.
Ortiz underwent an MRI over the weekend, with Murphy saying the structural results were good. However, the Brewers manager remains cautious because Ortiz is dealing with a bruised right knee and abdominal swelling.
Ortiz has not played since leaving Milwaukee's Sept. 25 game against the St. Louis Cardinals in the eighth inning.
Brewers Manager Pat Murphy said Andrew Vaughn is a full go this week, but they are still keeping an eye on Joey Ortiz’s abdomen and knee.
Murphy says Ortiz will be a “little limited” and they are keeping him from some of the higher intensity activities in today’s workout.
The Brewers have extra time to monitor Ortiz because their 103-59 regular season earned them a first-round bye. Milwaukee will open the NLDS on Oct. 3 against the winner of the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres Wild Card Series.
Ortiz was an important part of the Brewers' infield during the regular season. He appeared in 134 games and hit .270 with a .328 on-base percentage, .402 slugging percentage, nine home runs, 47 RBI and nine stolen bases.
Ortiz also recorded 100 hits, 14 doubles and four triples while drawing 35 walks. His availability could give Milwaukee another option in the infield as the team begins its postseason run.
For now, Murphy is giving Ortiz time rather than rushing him back into game action. The seven-day window between his last regular-season appearance and the NLDS gives the Brewers additional time to evaluate his condition.
Milwaukee enters October after winning 103 games, but Ortiz's health is one of the situations the team will continue monitoring before Game 1. His status should become clearer as the Brewers get closer to their postseason opener.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Bryce Harper lets Braves take lead with fielding blunder, makes up for it with game-tying HR next inning
item.dc:creator: Jason Owens
item.description: This was quite a sequence for Bryce Harper. With two men on and one out in a 1-1 game in the bottom of the seventh, Braves slugger Drake Baldwin hit a deep fly ball to right field. item.content:encoded:
This was quite a sequence for Bryce Harper.
With his Philadelphia Phillies facing elimination Wednesday against the Braves, the two-time MVP made a critical, late-game defensive blunder that allowed Atlanta to take the lead.
With two men on and one out in a 1-1 game in the bottom of the seventh, Braves slugger Drake Baldwin hit a deep fly ball to right field. Harper was in position to make the catch, but he misjudged the ball.
By the time he realized his mistake, it was too late. He backed up toward the warning track, but the ball bounced off his glove and over his head. The misplay allowed Sean Murphy to score from second for a 2-1 Atlanta lead.
The play was ruled a double, but it was clearly a mistake on Harper's part — one that he admitted in a postgame on-field interview with NBC. The Braves went on to take a 3-1 lead before the frame was done.
But given the chance, Harper immediately made up for his miscue at the plate.
Harper's teammate Kyle Schwarber led off the top of the eighth inning with a solo home run to cut Atlanta's lead to 3-2. One batter later, Harper followed with his own solo blast off Dylan Lee to tie the game 3-3.
The Phillies ultimately won 4-3 in the 10th after an Alec Bohm homer gave them the advantage in the top of the frame. They'll play a deciding Game 3 vs. the Braves on Thursday in Atlanta.
Harper has spent most of his career on defense in the outfield, but he has played primarily at first base or designated hitter since undergoing Tommy John surgery in 2022. When the Phillies traded for infielder Luis Arráez at the trade deadline this summer, Harper moved back to right field.
On Wednesday, it looked like he wasn't quite comfortable in that spot. But Harper has never been uncomfortable with the bat in his hand.

item.content:encoded:
The duality of Bryce Harper was on full display Wednesday afternoon in Atlanta.
In the span of six batters in the seventh inning, Harper badly misplayed a ball in right field that allowed the go-ahead run to cross the plate and hit a game-tying home run as part of back-to-back homers with Kyle Schwarber. Harper also drove in the game's first run with a single in the first inning. He went 2 for 5 in the Phillies' Game 2 win (PHI 4, ATL 3 in 10 innings).
"Schwarb, Harp, after we give up those two, they got momentum," Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly said. "And to be able to get that back right away was huge."
Philadelphia rearranged its defense to accommodate Luis Arraez at the trade deadline, which pushed Alec Bohm from third base to first base and Harper from first base back to right field. The results were not always positive. On Wednesday, Bohm failed to get an out on a bunt in that seventh inning immediately prior to Harper's misplay. Drake Baldwin lifted a fly ball that Harper misplayed into a double, which gave the Phillies a 2-1 lead.
"Obviously a world of emotion there," Harper said of his misplay. "I didn't think he hit it very hard and I realized he only hit 89 (mph exit velocity), so I thought it was going to be a pop fly just right at me and then it kind of kept traveling. Obviously a ball I should have caught."
Based on the exit velocity and launch angle, Statcast registered Baldwin's double -- "double" -- with an .080 expected batting average. Stats aside, it's a ball that must be caught, much like Ha-Seong Kim's bunt was a ball that had to be turned into an out. Bohm hesitated just enough for Sean Murphy to beat the throw to second base. Little things that cost the Phillies.
"I think it's a ball Bryce probably thinks he should have caught," Mattingly said. "It looked like it kept carrying a little bit. But no, you don't need to say anything to guys like that in that spot, not in this moment."
Matt Olson followed Baldwin's double -- again, "double" -- with a sacrifice fly to give the Braves a 3-1 lead in the seventh inning. The two misplays contributed directly to the two runs. Harper redeemed himself, though. He and Schwarber hit the back-to-back homers in the next half-inning to tie the game 3-3.
Those were the first two home runs Braves setup man Dylan Lee gave up to left-handed batters this season.
"Lee is our high-leverage lefty," Braves manager Walt Weiss said. "Put down the same part of the order yesterday pretty easily. Threw the ball really well yesterday. That's his inning every time."
Bohm redeemed himself as well. After botching the bunt, he hit a go-ahead home run in the top of the tenth inning, which stood up as the game-winning run thanks to Andrew Painter's heroic three-inning relief appearance. The Phillies have pulled even with the Braves in the Wild Card Series. The decisive Game 3 will be played Thursday afternoon.
"There's been a lot of ups and downs," Bohm said about his season. "Didn't start the best. I don't really know how to put it all into words quickly, but it's just been a long road with a lot of ups and downs. I've learned a lot, and I've made a lot of really close friends along the way and had a lot of people to lean on along the way. I really wouldn't have rather had it any other way."
To make the infield work with Arraez, the Phillies shifted Bryson Stott from second base to third, Bohm from third base to first, and Harper from first base to right. Prior to Arraez's arrival, Harper had not played the outfield since 2022. He moved to first base that summer to limit his throwing following his return from Tommy John surgery.
Arraez rolled his ankle at the end of the regular season and is not on the Wild Card Series roster. His status for the rest of the postseason, should the Phillies advance, is up in the air.

item.title: [sports.mynorthwest.com] Why Hyphen says Seattle Mariners need to extend Logan Gilbert - Seattle Sports
item.dc:creator: Zac Hereth
item.description: Why Hyphen says Mariners need to ink Logan Gilbert to extension Mariners analyst Ryan Rowland-Smith explains why keeping the right-hander is about more than just his performance. (Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) The Seattle Mariners have some heavy lifting to do this offseason as they attempt to bounce back from a disappointing 2026. In addition to a managerial search, the Mariners have a few key players set to hit free agency, namely left fielder Randy Arozarena and longtime shortstop J.P. Crawford.
item.content:encoded:
Why Hyphen says Mariners need to ink Logan Gilbert to extension
Mariners analyst Ryan Rowland-Smith explains why keeping the right-hander is about more than just his performance.
(Olivia Vanni/Getty Images)
The Seattle Mariners have some heavy lifting to do this offseason as they attempt to bounce back from a disappointing 2026.
In addition to a managerial search, the Mariners have a few key players set to hit free agency, namely left fielder Randy Arozarena and longtime shortstop J.P. Crawford. And beyond those the soon-to-be free agents, they could also have an interesting decision to make with starting pitcher Logan Gilbert on the horizon.
Gilbert, who has a career 3.60 ERA and 1,089 strikeouts over 1,021 1/3 innings in six big-league seasons, will be in his final year of club control in 2027 and figures to be one of the biggest names to hit free agency after that season.
Seattle has yet to come to terms on any sort of contract extension with Gilbert, and reports of any extension talks between he and the M’s have been sparse.
So, with Gilbert entering his final year of club control with the possibility that he could leave afterwards, is he a trade candidate this offseason? Mariners analyst and former MLB pitcher Ryan Rowland-Smith doesn’t think that is a route the club should go with Gilbert. During Monday’s edition of Seattle Sports’ Wyman and Bob, Rowland-Smith explained why the M’s should lock down their talented right-hander with a new deal.
Rowland-Smith pointed to the way Gilbert pitched in what was a meaningless Game 162 for the M’s in their season finale as an example of why Gilbert needs to be retained.
“You got a dude who wants to pitch in (Game) 162, and the way he came out, it was not some wave to the fans and thank you. He (brought) the same intensity (he normally would),” Rowland-Smith said. “You need him when you’ve got a Kade Anderson, Ryan Sloan and so on to say, ‘This is how we do things.'”
In that final outing of the season, Gilbert struck out eight batters over four perfect innings before allowing a leadoff walk in the fifth that ended his day.
“Many guys would just say I don’t need to pitch… just have a bullpen day,” Rowland-Smith said. “Do you know how many guys I’ve played with who would do that? Do not get rid of Logan Gilbert – 1,000%.”
The 29-year-old Gilbert was one of just 13 pitchers to strike out 200 batters this season. He was also one of just five to do so while pitching at least 180 innings. The Stetson product has pitched at least 180 innings in four of his five full seasons in the majors, with the lone exception being in 2025 when he made the only trip to the injured list in his career.
“Pay the man. Have him here for a long time because he is so valuable,” Rowland-Smith said. “Logan Gilbert, sometimes I take him for granted. He’s, again, in the clubhouse and in that dugout, he is gold with some of these young players who you plan to bring up.”
Hear the full conversation at this link or in the audio player in this story. Listen to Wyman and Bob weekdays from 2-7 p.m. or find the podcast on the Seattle Sports app.

item.content:encoded:
The Chicago White Sox chased Houston Astros ace Hunter Brown before the first inning ended in Game 2 of their AL wild-card series.
Brown was pulled for AJ Blubaugh after giving up four runs (three earned) on five hits in two-thirds of an inning. He faced all nine White Sox hitters and walked Colson Montgomery to turn the lineup over before leaving to a chorus of boos from the home crowd.
It's the first time in Brown's career that he's allowed more than one run in a playoff outing, whether as a starter or reliever.
Kyle Teel got the White Sox on the board with an RBI single to score leadoff hitter Sam Antonacci. Andrew Benintendi and Tristan Peters also had RBIs in the frame, and a third run scored on center fielder Lucas Spence's throwing error - one of two errors by Houston's defense in the inning.
Blubaugh limited the damage by getting Antonacci to ground out, stranding the bases loaded. That set the stage for Jeremy Peña to hit a leadoff homer off White Sox starter Sean Burke to cut Chicago's lead to 4-1.
This marks the second straight day an Astros starter failed to make it out of the opening frame. Blubaugh opened Game 1 in a designed bullpen game and gave up one run while loading the bases before Bryan King came in to clean it up. However, the one run Chicago scored off Blubaugh in Tuesday's first inning held up in a 6-3 White Sox win.
Houston - the first team in MLB history to win its division without a winning record - needs a victory Wednesday to extend its season and force a deciding Game 3 in the wild-card series.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees defeated the Boston Red Sox 9-0 at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx on Tuesday nigh.
They were led behind a dominant outing from right-handed ace Cam Schlittler and a six-RBI game from slugger Ben Rice.
Now, in Game 2 of the Wild Card Series on Wednesday night, the Yankees can punch their ticket to the ALDS with a win.
Left-hander Max Fried will take the mound for New York, while the Red Sox will send right-handed ace Sonny Gray to the mound.
With a righty on the mound, Yankees manager Aaron Boone made several changes to his starting lineup.
Yankees Announce Paul Goldschmidt Move
Among the moves Boone made, he removed veteran slugger Paul Goldschmidt from the lineup because he primarily uses him against lefties at this point in his career.
Goldschmidt ranks among the Yankees’ best hitters against lefties, but he’s struggled against righties, particularly Gray.
He’s 1-for-26 in his career against Gray with eight strikeouts and a double.
Luis Garcia Jr. will start at first base in place of Goldschmidt, while Rice will move up to the leadoff spot.
Here’s the Yankees starting lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Yankees 9/30 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF L. García Jr. 1B S. Jones RF G. Lombard Jr. SS J. Chisholm Jr. 2B T. Grisham CF A. Wells C R. McMahon 3B M. Fried SP.”
Yankees 9/30
B. Rice DH
C. Bellinger LF
L. García Jr. 1B
S. Jones RF
G. Lombard Jr. SS
J. Chisholm Jr. 2B
T. Grisham CF
A. Wells C
R. McMahon 3B
M. Fried SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 30, 2026
Looking at the Yankees Playoff Situation
The playoff bracket sends the winner of the Red Sox-Yankees series to face the No. 1-seeded Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS.
Game 1 of that series is scheduled for Saturday, so if the Yankees eliminate the Red Sox on Wednesday, New York will get two crucial days off.
If Boston wins, the two teams will have to play a win-or-go-home Game 3 on Thursday, where the Yankees would throw RHP Gerrit Cole and the Red Sox would pitch LHP Ranger Suarez.

As a result, Anthony will be replaced by Curtis Mead on Boston’s roster vs. New York Yankees in the American League Wild Card Series presented by AbbVie. Dr. Gary Green, MLB’s Medical Director, confirmed the injury after a full review of the medical information. MLB Postseason rules provide that a Club may request permission from the Comm
item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball announced today that it has approved a roster substitution for the Boston Red Sox due to an injury sustained by outfielder Roman Anthony. As a result, Anthony will be replaced by Curtis Mead on Boston’s roster vs. New York Yankees in the American League Wild Card Series presented by AbbVie. Dr. Gary Green, MLB’s Medical Director, confirmed the injury after a full review of the medical information.
MLB Postseason rules provide that a Club may request permission from the Commissioner’s Office to replace a player who is unable to play because of an injury. The Commissioner’s Office may approve or disapprove the request based on the specific facts and circumstances. In accordance with the rules, Anthony will be ineligible to return in the American League Division Series presented by Booking.com if the Red Sox participate, but he would be eligible to return for the American League Championship Series if Boston qualifies.
The Wild Card Series presented by AbbVie will be broadcast by NBC, Peacock and NBC Sports Network while ESPN Radio provides live national coverage. MLB Network will air extensive studio coverage throughout the Postseason across the Emmy Award-winning MLB Tonight, the Emmy-nominated MLB Central and MLB Now, and Intentional Talk, MLB Network’s longest-running talk show. Postseason games throughout 2026 will also be telecast in Spanish on Universo and Univision, while Univision Radio will provide Spanish language audio coverage. The 2026 Postseason will be distributed by MLB media rightsholders in 16 different languages to fans in more than 200 countries and territories.

item.title: [lanacion.com.ar] Thin MLB crowds in Atlanta, Houston show challenge of selling afternoon Wild Card Series tickets
item.description: Thin MLB crowds in Atlanta, Houston show challenge of selling afternoon Wild Card Series tickets A late home run secured a playoff win for Atlanta; stadium attendance remains low for scheduled weekday afternoon games - 1 minuto de lectura' Austin Riley delivered the first clutch moment of Major League Baseball's playoffs on Tuesday, hitting a go-ahead three-run homer in the eighth inning that pushed the Atlanta Braves over the Philadelphia Phillies for a 5-3 win . It was an electric scene for fa
item.content:encoded:
Thin MLB crowds in Atlanta, Houston show challenge of selling afternoon Wild Card Series tickets
A late home run secured a playoff win for Atlanta; stadium attendance remains low for scheduled weekday afternoon games
- 1 minuto de lectura'
Austin Riley delivered the first clutch moment of Major League Baseball's playoffs on Tuesday, hitting a go-ahead three-run homer in the eighth inning that pushed the Atlanta Braves over the Philadelphia Phillies for a 5-3 win .
It was an electric scene for fans at Truist Park — at least for those who decided to show up.
There has been a noticeable number of empty seats in Atlanta and Houston for day games during this week's Wild Card Series, with the Braves drawing 30,127 fans for Game 1 on Tuesday that started at 2 p.m. local time, well below the 41,108 capacity. The Astros announced that 34,011 fans attended Tuesday's 4 p.m. Game 1 at Daikin Park, also well below its 41,168-seat limit.
It's not the first time this has happened.
Since MLB permanently expanded the playoffs to a 12-team bracket in 2022, just six of 26 afternoon Wild Card Series games through Tuesday have reached or exceeded stadium capacity. Seven games failed to reach even 85% capacity. The Braves-Phillies game on Tuesday was 73.2% full, which is the lowest since the postseason expanded, according to research from Sportradar.
Game 2 of the Braves-Phillies series had an announced crowd of 37,150 on Wednesday.
The main issue for day games is obvious: It's hard for fans to attend day games during the week — particularly in late September and October — because people have to work and children are back in school. It doesn't help that those game times are announced with only a few days' notice.
Still, it's a less-than-ideal atmosphere for some of the most important contests of the year.
Phillies third baseman Alec Bohm shrugged off the smaller crowds before Wednesday's game, saying his team just wants to win games and advance.
“I don’t think anybody on our team is really focused on how many people are showing up here," Bohm said. "It’s just kind of -- I think, like you said, it’s a 2 o’clock game in the middle of the week, so I think that might have something to do with it.
“That doesn’t take away from what’s going on on the field and kind of the stakes of all that in our minds.”
All three ALWCS games in Cleveland last year between the Guardians and Detroit Tigers started at 1:08 p.m., and none drew more than 30,000 fans. The Tampa Bay Rays had just 19,704 for an ALWCS opener against Texas in 2023 that started at 3:08 p.m., the lowest attendance for a non-COVID MLB postseason game since the 1919 World Series.
MLB declined to comment on the attendance numbers, but the league spreads its wild-card games throughout the day on purpose so they have their own television window and capture the largest viewing audience possible. NBC is paying the league roughly $200 million per year to host “Sunday Night Baseball” and the Wild Card Series during a three-year deal agreed to last November.
The Astros fans who did attend Tuesday's game were in a bit of a foul mood, peppering the team with boos as they fell behind 5-0 by the fifth inning on the way to a 6-3 loss. Astros manager Joe Espada said he understood the fans' frustration but hoped for a better atmosphere on Wednesday.
“I do want our fans to know that we love them and we need them,” Espada said. “They’re part of what we are trying to accomplish here. They’re part of our family.”
AP Sports Writers Charles Odum in Atlanta and Kristie Rieken in Houston contributed to this story.
See AP’s full MLB coverage here

item.title: [yardbarker.com] Blue Jays planning to re-explore Japanese market this offseason
item.dc:creator: Vanessa Serrao
item.description: According to Toronto Blue Jays president and CEO Mark Shapiro, the team plans to re-explore the Japanese market this offseason. The Blue Jays will also be sending a contingency plan to Japan in the offseason, and Shapiro plans to travel there as they look to bolster the lineup. The Blue Jays have already been successful with recruiting Japanese star Kazuma Okamoto, who had a stellar rookie campaign this season with 33 home runs. On Sept. 8, he became the fifth Japanese-born player to hit 30 home
item.content:encoded:
According to Toronto Blue Jays president and CEO Mark Shapiro, the team plans to re-explore the Japanese market this offseason. The Blue Jays will also be sending a contingency plan to Japan in the offseason, and Shapiro plans to travel there as they look to bolster the lineup.
The Blue Jays have already been successful with recruiting Japanese star Kazuma Okamoto, who had a stellar rookie campaign this season with 33 home runs. On Sept. 8, he became the fifth Japanese-born player to hit 30 home runs, earning a noteworthy milestone achievement.
Signing Okamoto to a four-year, $60 million contract last offseason was a massive win. While the team's offense and power output took a significant step backward this season, Okamoto was the driving force behind the team's power. All things considered, his success has persuaded the team to continue to find more Japanese talent.
While the Blue Jays are targeting Seiya Suzuki from the Chicago Cubs as well, the team has also been eyeing two big Nippon Professional Baseball (NPB) stars who are expected to be on the market this winter and have already gained significant attention from MLB teams.
Mark Shapiro says the #BlueJays will send a contingency to Japan this offseason and he may travel there, too, as they look to expand their presence (both baseball and business).
He added that the Japanese market will obviously be something they explore again this winter.
Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato and right-handed pitcher Kaima Taira are two talents that would help enhance the Blue Jays' needs ahead of the 2027 season. Sato would provide the Blue Jays with an elite left-handed power bat who is coming off a dominant 37-home-run season with an explosive 1.012 OPS for the Hanshin Tigers.
With Taira, he is expected to be one of the top arms on the market alongside Tarik Skubal, who is an elite starter and reliever. But as a starter, he led all of NPB with a 1.36 ERA, serving as a commanding presence for the Saitama Seibu Lions.
The Blue Jays would benefit from adding his arm, as he would provide high-upside pitching depth to the rotation as well as a bullpen safety net. His versatility makes him an intriguing option to add as the team faced a heavily taxed pitching staff this season. While the Blue Jays are expected to get Cody Ponce, Bowden Francis and Jose Berrios back in 2027, you can never have enough pitching, and this past season proves it.

item.content:encoded:
Philadelphia Phillies right fielder Bryce Harper made a crucial mistake in Game 2 of the National League Wild Card Series against the Atlanta Braves at Truist Park.
With runners on first and second base and one out in the bottom of the seventh inning, Braves DH Drake Baldwin hit a deep fly ball to right field. Harper misplayed the ball, allowing Baldwin to reach on a double and a run to score, giving Atlanta a 2-1 lead.
The Braves added another run in the inning on a sacrifice fly from Matt Olson.
If the Phillies lose today, they will be eliminated from the postseason. If they come back, there will be a Game 3 tomorrow.
MLB World Reacts to Bryce Harper’s Defensive Gaffe in Phillies-Braves Game
@MattGelb: With the season in the balance, Bryce Harper misplays a ball in right field that is scored a double. The Phillies’ defense has hurt them all season; a fitting way for this to perhaps end. Cris Sánchez threw a career-high 116 pitches.

@BaseballWRLD_: BRYCE HARPER MIGHT HAVE JUST ENDED THE PHILLIES SEASON
@GrantPaulsen: Bryce Harper just misplayed a ball in right field allowing the Braves to take a two-run lead in the 8th inning. The Phillies are in big trouble.
Bryce Harper Redeems Himself
In the top of the eighth inning, Kyle Schwarber hit a solo home run, making it a 3-2 game.
Harper immediately followed with a game-tying solo home run.

UPDATE: Alec Bohm hit a go-ahed home run in the 10th inning. Phillies won 4-3.

item.title: [cubbiescrib.com] Alex Bregman's limitations are handcuffing Craig Counsell's Wild Card lineup decisions
item.dc:creator: Jordan Campbell
item.description: The fact that Alex Bregman is playing in games less than two weeks after taking a foul ball to the face and suffering multiple facial fractures is incredible, and while the Chicago Cubs are at their best with Bregman in the lineup, his current limitations have limited the flexibility Craig Counsell has elsewhere. Bregman served as the Cubs' designated hitter during their Game 1 loss to the San Diego Padres, and that's tied to the comfort level of him playing third base. When healthy, Bregman is
item.content:encoded:
The fact that Alex Bregman is playing in games less than two weeks after taking a foul ball to the face and suffering multiple facial fractures is incredible, and while the Chicago Cubs are at their best with Bregman in the lineup, his current limitations have limited the flexibility Craig Counsell has elsewhere.
Bregman served as the Cubs' designated hitter during their Game 1 loss to the San Diego Padres, and that's tied to the comfort level of him playing third base. When healthy, Bregman is arguably one of the best fielders at the hot corner in all of baseball. The problem is that while recovering from the aforementioned facial fractures, Bregman being relegated to DH duty limits the risk of further injury.
The problem that creates is with Pedro Ramirez at third base. Ramirez certainly has been an encouraging development for the Cubs this season, and while he's had offensive success this season, he's struggled against right-handed pitching.
Against righties this season, Ramirez is slashing .237/.298/.364 with a wRC+ of 82. To be clear, it's not like Counsell has a better option available to him. The other option, Matt Shaw, has also struggled against right-handed pitcher, boasting a wRC+ of 79 across 90 plate appearances this season.
Beyond the struggles that Ramirez and Shaw have had against right-handed pitchers this season, Bregman serving as the DH has forced Michael Conforto to the bench.
Cubs can't escape Alex Bregman dilemma that's complicating Craig Counsell's Wild Card lineup
Conforto has been used almost exclusively against right-haded pitchers this season. He has 302 plate appearances against righties this year, and only 11 against southpaws. In those 302 plate appearances, Conforto posted a 113 wRC+ with 29 extra-base hits.
No, Conforto likely wouldn't have made a difference in Game 1, that game quickly got away from the Cubs. But in looking for ways that Counsell could switch things up ahead of Game 2, one would think he would find a way to get the veteran into the lineup, especially since they will be facing the right-handed Nick Pivetta.
Of course, that may not be possible if Counsell doesn't feel comfortable with playing Bregman at third base. Bregman was taking reps at third base on Monday, and suggested that he would be capable of playing the field if asked. Facing an elimination game, perhaps it's cause for Counsell to step out of his comfort zone and force the issue with Bregman's return to third.

item.content:encoded:
By GLENN GUILBEAU, Tiger Rag Editor
The Pittsburgh Pirates were eliminated from the Major League Baseball Playoffs entering the last week of the regular season last week. That is 11 straight seasons for the franchise and third straight with franchise pitcher Paul Skenes – the No. 1 pick of the MLB Draft in 2023 from LSU.
The Pirates were better in 2026 than in Skenes’ first two seasons as Pittsburgh actually finished above .500 at 82-80 and in third place in the National League Central behind Milwaukee, which had the best regular season record in baseball at 103-59 and the Chicago Cubs at 89-73. Pittsburgh’s record would have been good enough to win the American League West, which Houston took at 81-81 to become the first team in MLB history to win a division with a non-winning record in a non-shortened season. The Texas Rangers were second at 80-82.
In 2025, the Pirates finished 71-91, and they were 76-86 in 2024.
When Skenes won National League Rookie of the Year in 2024 at 11-3 with a 1.96 ERA and started the first of two straight All-Star games, Pittsburgh averaged 1.35 runs a game with Skenes on the mound. In 2025 when Skenes took the National League Cy Young with a 10-10 mark and 1.96 ERA, he got 3.4 runs a game.
This season, Pittsburgh’s offense improved to 4.73 runs a game and 4.74 for Skenes, but he didn’t keep up his end. His ERA ballooned, for him, to 3.82 as he finished 10-11 on the season.
“Their ace’s struggles offered a reminder of one reason why a ticket won’t be punched,” Colin Beazley of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette wrote as the season neared the end.
The main reason for Skenes’ skid has been, according to most accounts, his drop in velocity from 98.8 as a rookie to 98.2 in 2025 and to 96.8 this season.
“It’s been frustrating,” Skenes told FOX Sports late in the season. “But the thing I’ve kind of realized is that I do everything I can. There’s an answer there somewhere. The velo is down. We see all the numbers. We can try to address it. We can do all that. To some extent, it’s kind of just how it is.”
Once the season ended last week, though, Skenes, 24, got a little more detailed in an exclusive interview with the Pittsburgh-Post Gazette and pointed to a variable. He pitched shortly before the season for Team USA in the World Baseball Classic last March, going 2-0 with a 1.08 ERA in eight and a third innings. That’s not a lot, and Skenes admitted to having some mechanical issues throughout the season. But he said he believes the pre-season WBC pitching may have triggered his issues in 2026 after no such pitching before his first two seasons.
“There are a lot of other factors, so I don’t want to put everything on the WBC,” Skenes told the Post-Gazette in an extensive interview published this past Monday. “But I feel like that was kind of the root of it a little bit. Usually, that time of year (in March at spring training), you’re kind of ramping up, and it’s a little bit slow. You can kind of get onto the slope and find your body. You’re topping at 97, and then the next you’re 98, 99. And that’s wasn’t the case this year. Looking back, I don’t think that (pitching in the WBC) really helped.”
Skenes’ average fastball velocity in the 2026 season was 96.8 mph, down from 98.1 in 2025 and 98.8 in 2024. His fastball dropped to a career “slow” 95.7 mph this past August in a game against Miami and averaged 96.1 in his last start on Sept. 25 against Kansas City.
His velocity was up and down through much of the season as was his consistency. He would have a poor outing, then a good one. He had three consecutive quality starts in mid-June. But from June 26 through August 5, he had a 6.26 ERA in eight starts with an uncharacteristic 3.9 walks per nine innings when his career average for walks was 2.2 per nine.
But even when he was pitching well, such as a 1.09 ERA over eight starts last April and May, he said something wasn’t right.
“Even then, I didn’t feel like I had my delivery,” Skenes told the Post-Gazette. “It’s just weird. It’s easier to kind of put your finger on it after the fact than it is in the moment.”
Skenes hopes to enter 2027 with no baggage.
“It definitely affected the year,” he said of pitching in the WBC. “It definitely didn’t make things easier.”
And sometimes little things make a difference.
“Everything is just having awareness of your hand at release,” Skenes told FOX shortly before the season ended. “It’s amazing how small things can be up the chain to throw that off. But looking at my assessments, nothing crazy has happened. What has happened this year, probably for that stretch in June through the beginning of August, was the velocity went down.”
That will obviously be what Skenes and the Pirates focus on before the 2027 season, which will be his first under the arbitration window. His contract runs out in the 2029 season.
“We’ll try to address it,” he said. “But you also have to understand what’s in your control and what’s not in your control. That was kind of not in my control. The velo goes up and down sometimes. Nothing has really explained my velocity drop. So, I’m not going to lose any sleep over it.”
That may be because of a conversation Skenes had with Detroit Tiger Justin Verlander late in the season. Verlander, a 10-time All-Star, five-time strikeout leader and three-time Cy Young winner who was the 2006 rookie of the year, announced during the 2026 season that ’26 would be his last at age 43.
Verlander told Skenes that his velocity mysteriously dropped in his third full season at Detroit in 2008 as Skenes did in his third year in 2026.
“He was like, ‘My third year, I just lost my velo. I was completely healthy. It kind of just went away, and then it came back,’” Skenes said.
The Baseball Savant velocity tracker confirmed Verlander dropped to 94.3 in his third season in 2008, then rose to 96.3 in 2009 and remained up through most of his career.
“I was like, ‘You know what? That’s kind of good to hear,’” Skenes said he told Verlander. “It’s not just me.”
And it likely was, partly, the WBC action.

item.content:encoded:
La trayectoria de Jonathan Aranda representa un recorrido destacado desde el beisbol infantil de Tijuana hasta los escenarios más importantes de las Grandes Ligas. El tijuanense pasó de formarse en los campos de la Liga Municipal de Tijuana a convertirse en pieza fundamental de los Tampa Bay Rays, equipo que aseguró su lugar en las Series Divisionales de los Playoffs de la MLB.
Durante la temporada regular 2026, Aranda tuvo un papel protagonista dentro de la ofensiva de Tampa Bay. El primera base e infielder mostró consistencia con el bate y terminó la campaña con un promedio de .277, además de sumar 156 imparables, 22 cuadrangulares y 92 carreras producidas, cifras que reflejan su importancia en el orden ofensivo de los Rays.
Su rendimiento fue determinante para que Tampa Bay alcanzara los playoffs con la mira puesta en avanzar a las siguientes rondas. Para Aranda, la clasificación representa otro paso importante en una carrera que comenzó en el beisbol tijuanense y que ahora lo coloca frente a uno de los mayores retos de su trayectoria. Aquí en Heraldo Deportes te contamos sus inicios y cómo llegó a Grandes Ligas.
Así fueron los humildes inicios de Jonathan Aranda en el beisbol de Tijuana
Jonathan Aranda encontró en el béisbol una oportunidad para mantenerse alejado de los entornos de violencia en Tijuana y construir un camino ligado al deporte. Nacido el 23 de mayo de 1998 en Baja California, comenzó a jugar desde pequeño con el respaldo de sus padres, Humberto Aranda y Ventura, quienes veían en esta actividad una forma de fomentar la disciplina y mantenerlo protegido. Con el paso de los años, aquella iniciativa familiar se convirtió en el inicio de una carrera que lo llevaría hasta las Grandes Ligas.
Durante su infancia, Aranda desarrolló su talento en las ligas infantiles y juveniles de Tijuana, donde destacó especialmente en la Liga Municipal. En esos campos también forjó una amistad con Alejandro Kirk, otro pelotero tijuanense que alcanzaría el máximo nivel del béisbol profesional. Ambos compartieron sus primeros pasos en el diamante y, con el tiempo, transformaron aquellos años de formación en una trayectoria que los llevaría a representar a México en la MLB.
Te puede interesar: Playoffs MLB 2026: Así puedes VER EN VIVO los juegos entre Yankees y Red Sox de Grandes Ligas
La historia de cómo Jonathan Aranda llegó a Grandes Ligas
El camino profesional de Jonathan Aranda comenzó con los Toros de Tijuana, donde fue identificado como uno de los jóvenes talentos de la región. El tijuanense pasó cerca de dos años dentro del sistema de desarrollo del club, trabajando principalmente en su capacidad de contacto y preparación ofensiva. En 2016 tuvo actividad con los Toros de Moroleón en la Liga Invernal Mexicana, una etapa que le permitió adquirir experiencia y llamar la atención de organizaciones de Grandes Ligas.
Su oportunidad con los Tampa Bay Rays surgió durante una sesión de visoría realizada en Tijuana en 2015. Los cazatalentos habían acudido para observar a Randy Arozarena, quien entrenaba con los Toros, y terminaron siguiendo de cerca el desempeño de Aranda. El bateador tijuanense convenció por su técnica y capacidad ofensiva, por lo que los Rays decidieron firmarlo por un bono de 130 mil dólares, dando inicio a su recorrido por las ligas menores. Siete años después, en 2022, Aranda debutó en la MLB y comenzó una nueva etapa de su carrera en el máximo nivel del béisbol.

item.content:encoded:
Pete Crow-Armstrong and his Chicago Cubs will square off against the San Diego Padres in Game 2 of the NL Wild Card at Petco Park, on Wednesday, Sept. 30 at 10 p.m. ET. Crow-Armstrong has +300 odds to hit a home run as of Wednesday afternoon.
What It Means
Crow-Armstrong is hitting for a .280 BA, .372 OBP and .570 SLG with a 25.8% strikeout rate and an 11.4% walk rate. His OPS is .943, which ranks 2nd in MLB, and he has scored 119 runs. In 726 plate appearances, he has hit 45 home runs (1st in MLB) and driven in 107 runs (4th in MLB). Crow-Armstrong has recorded 41 steals on 48 attempts. He had a hitless showing in his previous game (0 for 3) against the Padres.
The Padres will send Nick Pivetta (3-2) out to make his ninth start of the season. He is 3-2 with a 2.86 ERA and 42 strikeouts in 34 2/3 innings pitched.

item.content:encoded:
The MLB Wild Card Series presented by AbbVie begins on Tuesday, and all games in this round will be available exclusively on NBC platforms.
Each series will be a best of three, meaning there will be four games on Tuesday, another four games on Wednesday and up to four games on Thursday depending on how many series go the distance.
As you prepare for what will be a thrilling postseason, here’s what you need to know to make sure you are ready to tune in from the jump.
Quick guide to watching the Wild Card Series on NBC and Peacock
- Wild Card games will be available this year on NBC platforms.
- All Wild Card games will be available on Peacock Premium or Premium Plus (descriptions available here).
- Peacock is available across a variety of devices. To get started, find or download the Peacock application on your device or head directly to PeacockTV.com to create a Peacock account.
- For questions on how to sign up and access via your device you can reference Peacock's Getting Started Page.
- Games available on NBC broadcast will also be available on Peacock.
- Games that are not available on NBC broadcast will be available on Peacock and also on NBC Sports Network (NBCSN).
- NBCSN is available on YouTube TV, Fubo and Xfinity.
Wild Card Series broadcast teams
- Phillies @ Braves: Matt Vasgersian, John Kruk, C.J. Nitkowski, Joey Votto, Ashley ShahAhmadi
- White Sox @ Astros: Tom McCarthy, Steve Stone, Geoff Blum, Adam Ottavino, Britney Eurton
- Red Sox @ Yankees: Jason Benetti, Lou Merloni, Joe Girardi, Anthony Rizzo, Caroline Pineda
- Cubs @ Padres: Dave Flemming, Jim Deshaies, Mark Grant, Clayton Kershaw, John Fanta
The full schedule is below (all times are ET)
Peacock subscribers can click on the links below to go directly to the stream of that game.
TUESDAY, SEPT. 29 -- WILD CARD SERIES GAME 1
WEDNESDAY, SEPT. 30 -- WILD CARD SERIES GAME 2
THURSDAY, OCT. 1 -- WILD CARD SERIES GAME 3

Three-Game Scenarios
If Phillies vs. Braves series is over:
White Sox @ Astros: 2 p.m. on NBC & Peacock
Red Sox @ Yankees: 8 p.m. on NBC & Peacock
Cubs @ Padres: 10 p.m. on Peacock & NBCSN
If Cubs vs. Padres series is over:
Phillies @ Braves: 2 p.m. on NBC & Peacock
White Sox @ Astros: 5 p.m. on Peacock & NBCSN
Red Sox @ Yankees: 8 p.m. on NBC & Peacock
If Red Sox vs. Yankees series is over:
Phillies @ Braves: 2 p.m. on NBC & Peacock
White Sox @ Astros: 5 p.m. on Peacock & NBCSN
Cubs @ Padres: 8 p.m. on Peacock & NBCSN

Red Sox @ Yankees: 7 p.m. on NBC & Peacock
Cubs @ Padres: 9:30 p.m. on NBC & Peacock
IF CWS@HOU and CHC@SD are over:

Red Sox @ Yankees: 8 p.m. on NBC & Peacock
Any One-Game Scenario
If Thursday, Oct. 1, has only one Game 3, then it will be played at 8 p.m. on NBC and Peacock
NBC and MLB go way back
NBC has a long history with MLB. The first MLB broadcast on TV was a 1939 Cincinnati Reds-Brooklyn Dodgers doubleheader on W2XBS (the precursor to WNBC-TV) in New York. NBC Sports was the home to the first World Series broadcast in 1947, the first All-Star Game nationally broadcast in 1952 and has televised 39 World Series -- more than any other network.
From 1957-2000, NBC Sports was home to a wealth of baseball programming, including Game of the Week and Monday Night Baseball telecasts, more than 30 All-Star Games and countless iconic postseason moments. MLB Sunday Leadoff -- a first-of-its-kind Sunday morning presentation featuring a unique three-announcer broadcast booth with one analyst with expertise on each team joining play-by-play voice Jason Benetti -- returned to NBC and Peacock this season after previously airing on Peacock during the 2022-23 seasons.

item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball announced the broadcast schedule for the 2026 Wild Card Series presented by AbbVie. The 2026 postseason will begin with each of the four Wild Card Series scheduled from Tuesday through Thursday under a best-of-three format, all available across NBC Sports platforms, including NBC, Peacock and NBC Sports Network. Coverage of the Wild Card Series marks the return of postseason baseball to NBC for the first time since the 2000 ALCS.
The Wild Card Series will be available in Spanish on Universo, while Univision Radio will provide Spanish language audio coverage. ESPN Radio will provide live national coverage of all 2026 MLB postseason games, beginning with the Wild Card Series. In addition, MLB Network will air extensive studio coverage throughout the postseason across the Emmy Award-winning MLB Tonight, the Emmy-nominated MLB Central and MLB Now, and Intentional Talk, MLB Network’s longest-running talk show.

item.content:encoded:
The MLB playoffs are in full swing, as Wild Card matchups began this week.
For the Los Angeles Dodgers, they are still awaiting their opponent for the NLDS. It will be either the Atlanta Braves or the Philadelphia Phillies.
Amid the MLB playoffs, the Dodgers made a few roster moves in preparation for their upcoming series.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Announce Tyler Mahle News After Dramatic Phillies Game
Los Angeles Dodgers Make 3 Roster Changes
The Dodgers do know that they will begin their quest for a three-peat on Saturday, October 3.
In the meantime, here are the three roster moves the team made, per the team’s transactions tracker:
“Los Angeles Dodgers activated RHP Edgardo Henriquez from the 15-day injured list.”
“Los Angeles Dodgers recalled LHP Ronan Kopp from Oklahoma City Comets.”
“Los Angeles Dodgers recalled SS Hyeseong Kim from Oklahoma City Comets.”
The most notable roster move of the trio is Edgardo Henriquez being activated from the 15-day IL, which could be a huge boost to the Dodgers’ bullpen. However, he still needs to be announced on the Dodgers’ NLDS roster, which has not been made public yet.
As for Hyeseong Kim, he could be a pinch-runner option if the Dodgers opt to go that route.
More MLB on Heavy: Chicago Cubs Announce Interesting Seiya Suzuki Decision Before MLB Playoffs
What Do Roster Moves Mean for Los Angeles Dodgers Playoff Chances?
If Henriquez can go for the Los Angeles Dodgers’ relief corps, that is a huge boost because he has been one of the team’s breakout pitchers and a highly dependable reliever.
As for the other two moves, they might not be noticeable now, but could play a role down the line.
Ronan Kopp being recalled to the 40-man roster is likely in case of an emergency, but if the Dodgers advance past the NLDS, there’s a slight chance he could be added to the official postseason roster.
Hyeseong Kim is a player who could pay slight dividends on the bases if manager Dave Roberts opts to use him in the late innings as a pinch-runner option.

item.dc:creator: Javier Noriega
item.description: Con batazos de cuatro esquinas de Fernando Tatis Jr., Manny Machado y Xander Bogaerts, sumados a una joya monticular de Michael King, San Diego se impuso 8-0 a Chicago para ponerse a un triunfo de la Serie Divisional. Los dominicanos Fernando Tatis Jr. y Manny Machado fueron protagonistas en la victoria de San Diego. Foto: MLB. 30 de septiembre de 2026 Hora: 15:43 Padres de San Diego defendió con autoridad su feudo en el primer encuentro de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Nacional, tras imponers
item.content:encoded:
Con batazos de cuatro esquinas de Fernando Tatis Jr., Manny Machado y Xander Bogaerts, sumados a una joya monticular de Michael King, San Diego se impuso 8-0 a Chicago para ponerse a un triunfo de la Serie Divisional.
Los dominicanos Fernando Tatis Jr. y Manny Machado fueron protagonistas en la victoria de San Diego. Foto: MLB.
30 de septiembre de 2026 Hora: 15:43
Padres de San Diego defendió con autoridad su feudo en el primer encuentro de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Nacional, tras imponerse con una contundente blanqueada de 8-0 sobre Cachorros de Chicago en el Petco Park. La novena californiana cimentó su victoria gracias a una electrizante exhibición ofensiva liderada por Fernando Tatis Jr. y una sobresaliente apertura del derecho Michael King.
El ataque de los frailes no se hizo esperar y castigó temprano al abridor de Chicago, Matthew Boyd. En la conclusión del primer episodio, el poder dominicano se hizo sentir en todo el estadio: Tatis Jr. inauguró la pizarra al depositar la esférica en las gradas del jardín central, seguido por otro cuadrangular de Manny Machado entre los prados izquierdo y derecho. La ofensiva continuó en el tercer capítulo, cuando el antesalista conectó un doblete contra la barda que bañó al jardinero Pete Crow-Armstrong para remolcar a su compatriota y ampliar la ventaja a 3-0.
El arubeño Xander Bogaerts se unió al festín ofensivo contra el zurdo de Cachorros, despachando un dantesco cuadrangular solitario que aterrizó en las gradas del jardín izquierdo. El asedio de San Diego se profundizó en la quinta entrada, cuando Jackson Merrill conectó un sencillo remolcador de dos anotaciones que puso el marcador 6-0. En ese mismo episodio, Ty France pisó la registradora para sumar la séptima rayita del encuentro, aprovechando un pasbol del receptor Carson Kelly.
Más allá de la demostración de poder, Fernando Tatis Jr. demostró otra de las herramientas de su repertorio: la velocidad en las almohadillas. El jardinero causó estragos en la defensiva visitante al estafarse la intermedia y, apoyado en un errático tiro de Kelly hacia la segunda base, completó una fantástica y agresiva carrera hasta el plato para sellar el 8 – 0 definitivo.
Desde el montículo, Michael King maniató por completo a los maderos rivales. El diestro se adjudicó la victoria tras lanzar siete entradas en blanco, en las que apenas toleró un indiscutible, otorgó tres pasaportes y retiró a ocho bateadores por la vía del ponche.
LEA TAMBIÉN:
La serie al mejor de tres compromisos continuará esta noche a las 10:00 p.m., cuando ambas novenas vuelvan a saltar al diamante. Para este duelo crucial, Cachorros de Chicago dependerá de los envíos del derecho Kevin Gausman, quien subirá a la lomita con la obligación de evitar la eliminación. Por su parte, Padres de San Diego le entregarán la esférica a Nick Pivetta, quien tendrá la misión de definir la serie y sellar el pase a la Serie Divisional.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Edwin Diaz Committed to "Earning" Spot on Postseason Roster
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — Edwin Díaz knows exactly what is at stake over the final days of the regular season. After an injury-plagued year and an uneven return to the majors, the veteran reliever is trying to convince the Dodgers that he belongs in their postseason bullpen. Saturday brought another encouraging step in that direction. Díaz worked a scoreless inning against the Giants and, more importantly, came away feeling that the fastball command that had eluded him earlier in the season is finally b
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Edwin Díaz knows exactly what is at stake over the final days of the regular season.
After an injury-plagued year and an uneven return to the majors, the veteran reliever is trying to convince the Dodgers that he belongs in their postseason bullpen. Saturday brought another encouraging step in that direction.
Díaz worked a scoreless inning against the Giants and, more importantly, came away feeling that the fastball command that had eluded him earlier in the season is finally back.
“Yeah, 100%,” Díaz said when asked if he feels better now than he did before his latest stint in Triple-A. “I’ve been able to throw strikes. I think that was my problem, my concern. I wasn’t throwing my fastball for strikes. Now I’m able to command my fastball really good. And when I command my fastball, my slider plays up.”
That relationship between the two pitches is critical for Díaz. When the fastball is located properly, hitters have a much tougher time distinguishing it from his slider before the breaking ball dives away.
“Right now it’s really good,” Díaz said of the slider. “It’s going down and away. I’ve been able to throw my fastball glove side, so if I throw my fastball glove side, the slider will play off the same path.”
Díaz believes the improvement traces back to a mechanical adjustment made during his time at Oklahoma City.
Following a rough Triple-A appearance, he sat down with the pitching coaches and identified an issue with his hip movement and posture. He said the correction also helped restore an arm slot that had drifted earlier in the season.
“We found I wasn’t moving my hips the right way,” Díaz said. “We started working on that. On Tuesday I threw a really good pen. On Wednesday I pitched, I felt great, and lately I’ve been really good.”
The Dodgers have also been able to ease Díaz back into major league competition without immediately asking him to protect one-run leads in the ninth inning. He said he is perfectly comfortable with that arrangement.
“I’m open-minded right here,” Díaz said. “I need to help this team win. Whatever Doc puts me in the game, in any situation, I will do my job. I feel good. I just want to keep climbing the ladder and finish the season strong.”
That ladder could eventually lead to an October roster spot, but Díaz knows nothing has been guaranteed.
Dave Roberts has acknowledged that there is competition for the final places in a crowded Dodgers bullpen, and Díaz understands that his performance over these final games matters.
“I got to show them that I’m part of that bullpen,” Díaz said. “I haven’t pitched this year, and when I’ve been in the majors, I’ve been struggling. So right now I’m giving my 200% just to show them I will be in that roster spot.”
For Díaz, the path from here is simple: keep throwing strikes, keep getting clean innings, and give the Dodgers a reason to trust him in October.
“Every time they give me the ball, in any situation, I will do my job,” he said. “And then at the end of the season, they will make decisions.”

A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.title: [si.com] Ronald Acuna Jr. Makes Braves History with Stolen Base Feat

item.description: The Atlanta Braves are one win away from a trip to the National League Division Series and a date with the back-to-back World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers. They fell into an early 1-0 hole against the Philadelphia Phillies in Game 2 of the NL wild card series, but that didn't stop star outfielder Ronald Acuna Jr. from doing something special that has only been done twice in Braves history. With the Braves down 1-0, Acuna stole two bases in the bottom of the first inning and ultimately sco
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves are one win away from a trip to the National League Division Series and a date with the back-to-back World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers. They fell into an early 1-0 hole against the Philadelphia Phillies in Game 2 of the NL wild card series, but that didn't stop star outfielder Ronald Acuna Jr. from doing something special that has only been done twice in Braves history.
With the Braves down 1-0, Acuna stole two bases in the bottom of the first inning and ultimately scoring the team's first run on Matt Olson's RBI single to tie the game up. According to Sarah Langs of MLB.com, Acuna has joined two Braves legends on an all-exclusive list.
Ronald Acuna Jr. makes Braves history
Acuna has also become the seventh player in postseason history with two stolen bases in the first inning of a game. That was last done by Phillies star shortstop Trea Turner in Game 2 of the NL Division Series against the New York Mets.
But it still has been a very long time since a member of the Braves accomplished this feat. Rafael Furcal was last with the Braves in 2005, so it has been over two decades since a Braves player has pulled this off.
Acuna is a former MVP, NL Rookie of the Year, three-time Silver Slugger and five-time All-Star. He is signed through this season and has club options for 2027 and 2028.
During the regular season, the 28-year-old outfielder hit .255/.345/.451 with 20 home runs, 55 RBI, 21 stolen bases and a .796 OPS. Injuries limited him to 107 games, but he has started the postseason off with a bang and is a big reason why the Braves are now pointed towards the NLDS.
But along with his power and solid defense has come some elite speed and baserunning, and he put that on full display in Game 2 as the Braves punched back from an early deficit against the Phillies and put themselves in position to potentially advance to the next round.
The postseason is always full of historic moments, and Acuna created one of his own with his speed on the basepaths. It will be interesting to see if the Braves can ultimately take Game 2 and effectively end the Phillies' season. A win advances them to the next round.
The game is currently tied at one apiece in the fourth inning.
Curt Bishop is a freelance sports writer who graduated from Maryville University of St. Louis with a Bachelor of Arts degree in the field of Communication and currently writes as a contributor for various platforms covering Major League Baseball. item.content:encoded:
Una jornada decisiva llega rápidamente a los Playoffs 2026 de las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol (MLB) este miércoles 30 de septiembre cuando los Yankees se enfrenten a los Red Sox durante el Juego 2 de la Serie de Comodines en el Yankee Stadium, partido que los Medias Rojas buscarán ganar a toda costa para mantenerse con vida y forzar a un decisivo tercer desafío. Aquí te decimos dónde ver el juego de hoy EN VIVO.
Aaron Boone y los Yankees vuelven al terreno, probablemente, después de su mejor juego de playoffs en años al mostrar una tórrida ofensiva y un pitcheo de lujo ante unos Red Sox que necesitan sacudirse la derrota de inmediato para llevar esta serie del Wild Card hasta sus máximas consecuencias.
Te Recomendamos
¿Cómo llegan al juego Yankees y Red Sox HOY?
Los New York Yankees están arriba 1-0 en esta Serie de Comodines de la Liga Americana, con la primera victoria a su favor para avanzar a la Serie Divisional. Durante el juego de esta noche, los Yankees buscarán replicar la fórmula y eliminar a sus más acérrimos rivales por segundo año consecutivo; la postemporada anterior perdieron el primer juego antes de quedarse con los dos siguientes, convirtiéndose apenas en el tercer equipo de 24 que remonta en una Serie de Comodines.
All gas, no brakes. #RepBX pic.twitter.com/N0ndrDDBHK
— New York Yankees (@Yankees) September 30, 2026
Los Boston Red Sox esperan protagonizar otro gran regreso, como el que en la temporada regular les permitió conseguir un boleto a los playoffs luego de un terrible inicio. La gran fortaleza esta noche para los Red Sox es su pitcheo, mismo que esta noche estará a cargo de Sonny Gray (18-5, 2.72). El diestro dominó a los Yankees con dos salidas de calidad.

item.title: [MLB.com] Pivetta tabbed to start Game 2 after missing most of 2026 with right elbow injury
item.dc:creator: Cole Bradley
item.description: SAN DIEGO -- Through Nick Pivetta’s first four starts this season, it was clear he was picking up right where he left off from his career-best 2025 campaign, one that saw him finish sixth in National League Cy Young Award voting … only for it to be derailed by a right elbow injury in April that cost him nearly five months. item.content:encoded:
SAN DIEGO -- Through Nick Pivetta’s first four starts this season, it was clear he was picking up right where he left off from his career-best 2025 campaign, one that saw him finish sixth in National League Cy Young Award voting … only for it to be derailed by a right elbow injury in April that cost him nearly five months.
But upon his return on Sept. 7, Pivetta reassumed the version of himself that was prevalent throughout last year, putting a lengthy rehab behind him and leaving no doubt that he was fully ready to contribute on the biggest stage.
This time, though, he’ll have the Petco Park crowd behind him.
“We're very lucky to have such a great fan base here,” Pivetta said. “From what I've heard from the guys that have played here before, I'm expecting great things and very excited for it. Just trying to keep all my focus on the game, but enjoy those moments, too, with those fans and try to bring the championship home for them.”
Since returning from the injured list, Pivetta has looked a lot like the guy who posted a 2.87 ERA across 31 starts in ‘25. He allowed a mere three runs over 18 2/3 innings over four starts, good for a 1.45 ERA. He delivered 4 2/3 scoreless frames against the Dodgers in Los Angeles his last time out, helping the Padres secure their third consecutive trip to the postseason that night.
“High level of confidence with Nick, what a road he’s been on this year,” Padres manager Craig Stammen said. “For him, when it didn’t look great at the beginning of the season, to put in the work over an entire season and not know if he’s ever going to get back … now he’s [been] one of our best pitchers down the stretch.”
The four-start runway Pivetta had allowed him to build up to full pitch count (he threw 87 pitches in his last start), meaning there should be zero limitations for him this postseason.
Of course, the Padres almost certainly won’t need him to go a full four or five innings, given their elite bullpen that was pieced together specifically to help shorten games in the playoffs -- a formula that San Diego has deployed with great success in its previous seasons and seems poised to do once more.
But Pivetta’s postseason track record is nothing to scoff at.
He was brilliant for the Red Sox during their playoff run in 2021 that saw him come out of the bullpen in the American League Division Series against the Rays before he twirled five innings of one-run ball against the eventual World Series champion Astros in Game 4 of the AL Championship Series. And, of course, he held the Cubs to just two runs over five innings and struck out nine in Game 1 of the Wild Card Series last year, capping off an excellent first season in San Diego.
That Chicago lineup will be a little different this time -- much stronger, for one. He’ll have to navigate a top of the order that includes the likely NL MVP in center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and a surging Alex Bregman, who posted a 1.010 OPS in the second half.
“It's a whole lineup; they make good contact, they don't swing outside of the zone,” Pivetta said. “They have guys in there that jell really well together, led by Bregman. It's just trying to keep them off-balance, but always sticking to my strengths and doing what I do best and just see where that night goes.”
Pivetta is up for the challenge.
“I'm healthy, I'm feeling good and I'm excited for the next step,” he said.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have yet to begin their quest for a three-peat during these MLB playoffs, which are already underway, but on paper, LA is going to be a tough out regardless of its opponent.
However, even though the MLB playoffs are underway, it’s not too early to start thinking about the major offseason decision the team faces regarding ace starter Tarik Skubal.
Recently, in an MLB free agent predictions piece, Tarik Skubal is being linked back to the Los Angeles Dodgers on a 10-year deal.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce 3 Sudden Roster Moves Amid MLB Playoffs
Dodgers Predicted to Retain Tarik Skubal
Back in August, the Dodgers shocked the MLB world by landing Tarik Skubal in a huge trade with the Detroit Tigers.
However, they (LA) face a big decision regarding his free-agent status, as he is set to hit the open market after the 2026 season.
BleacherReport.com’s Zach Buckley recently predicted LA to retain its new ace via a 10-year deal:
“Prediction: Skubal re-signs with the Dodgers on a 10-year deal.”
“In short, the crystal ball sees this coming down to the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets—two of the biggest spenders in baseball. The Dodgers just made an aggressive move for Skubal at this year’s trade deadline, while the Mets badly need a boost to their rotation. This bidding war should be ferocious, but in the end, the Dodgers’ head start by having Skubal already on the roster could be what pushes them over the edge.”
More MLB on Heavy: MLB World Reacts to Austin Riley Moment in Phillies-Braves Game
Tarik Skubal Has Proved His Worth with Los Angeles
Let’s be clear: the 2X AL Cy Young winner in Tarik Skubal, doesn’t have to prove his worth to anybody, but since joining the Dodgers, he’s made it really hard for the team to ignore that he would be an immense addition to the starting rotation.
Across 10 starts with LA, Skubal holds a 2.61 ERA with 70 strikeouts.
He will be a huge piece to the Dodgers postseason fold, and if he really helps propel LA to a three-peat, that might be enough to truly force Andrew Friedman’s hand in his ongoing contract talks.
Dodgers fans, do you want to bring back Tarik Skubal? And at what price would you be willing to do so?
