item.content:encoded:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Pirates won't finish the 2026 season with playoff baseball and it's a let down for every player, especially Paul Skenes.
The Pirates' starting pitcher, who ended his third MLB season, hasn't been a part of a postseason team yet, with the 2026 team eliminated a week ago.
Skenes and the Pirates did avoid a losing season, but the ace is done with coming up short and wants to be a part of a playoff squad, something he envisions in Pittsburgh.
"That's cool. We all wanted to play in October," Skenes said. "Like I said, I think our best baseball is ahead of us, I thought there was a lot of kind of unfortunate stuff that happened this year. Stuff that was just out of our control. Guys getting hurt and stuff like that. I think it'd be a different picture if stuff like that didn't happen. So it's tough.
"This is my third year, and every year, at the end, we’re talking about ‘What’s it going to look like for next year,’ and I’m tired of it. We are in a good position for next year, I know that, but it’s gonna be tough to think about that again for a whole offseason.”
Skenes Hoping For Better in 2027
The Pirates were competitive throughout the 2026 season and can clinch a winning season with a win in their final two games against the Detroit Tigers at Comerica Park, on either Sept. 26 or Sept. 27.
Pittsburgh last had a winning season in 2018, 82-79, and hasn't made the postseason since 2015, the second-longest streak in baseball to the Los Angeles Angels (2014).
The Pirates have had little success in recent history, with this just the fifth non-losing season in the past 34 years, with three postseason appearances from 2013-15 and a record 20 straight losing seasons from 1993-2012.
2026 was a much better season for the Pirates, who put together a roster that had postseason potential.
The Pirates had one of the best lineups in baseball before the All-Star break, with offseason additions in second baseman Brandon Lowe and slugger Ryan O'Hearn excelling, internal improvements from center fielder Oneil Cruz, left fielder Bryan Reynolds, first baseman Spencer Horwitz, catcher Endy Rodríguez and third baseman Nick Gonzales, plus breakout rookies in shortstop Konnor Griffin and right fielder Esmerlyn Valdez.
Pittsburgh fell short of their goal due to injuries to their best hitters, a bullpen that struggled and a starting rotation that was inconsistent.
The Pirates have a much better bullpen following the trade deadline and a starting rotation that should be in a better position next season, so there is reason for optimism that they can finally break through.
"I don't know, and that's going to be another off-season thing," Skenes said about what the Pirates need to do next season. "You know, I don't. I don't think there's anything that needs to be completely overhauled."
Skenes Faces Important Offseason
Skenes has a big offseason, himself, after falling short of his National League Cy Young Award season in 2025.
He posted a 10-11 record in 32 starts, a 3.82 ERA over 174.1. innings pitched, 200 strikeouts to 49 walks, a .227 BAA and a 1.12 WHIP.
Skenes' ERA was almost twice what it was last season, although his expected ERA (3.28) was 10th-best in baseball.
There were some mechanical issues and a drop in velocity for Skenes this season, as well as an early start due to the World Baseball Classic, but with a full offseason ahead of him, he's confident he can fix those issues and help lead the Pirates back to the postseason in 2027.
“I think my best baseball is ahead of me, and I think our best baseball is ahead of us," Skenes said. "Got a long offseason and have the chance to sit down and look at all the stuff. It’s really easy to get emotional and kind of let emotions bleed into some stuff during the season. To be able to sit back and kinda look at the big picture rather than the day-to-day, short-term view of it that takes over in-season, that will be good.”
Dominic writes for Pittsburgh Pirates On SI, Pittsburgh Panthers Pn SI and also, Pittsburgh Steelers On SI. A Pittsburgh native, Dominic grew up watching Pittsburgh Sports and wrote for The Pitt News as an undergraduate at the University of Pittsburgh, covering Pitt Athletics. He would write for Pittsburgh Sports Now after college and has years of experience covering sports across Pittsburgh.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Why Ronald Acuña Jr. Might Be the Exception to Alex Anthopoulos's Rule
item.dc:creator: Roman Janeiro; Unknown
item.description: Ronald Acuña Jr. continues to be one of the hottest hitters in baseball this September, hitting .342 with an OPS approaching 1.100. That late-season run got even more impressive over the weekend, when he locked up a 20/20 season despite missing more than 50 games to injury — the third time in his career he's cleared 20 home runs in a season shortened by at least 50 missed games. Acuña hasn't just been one of the best hitters in baseball this month; he's reminded everyone he's one of the sport's
item.content:encoded:
Ronald Acuña Jr. continues to be one of the hottest hitters in baseball this September, hitting .342 with an OPS approaching 1.100. That late-season run got even more impressive over the weekend, when he locked up a 20/20 season despite missing more than 50 games to injury — the third time in his career he's cleared 20 home runs in a season shortened by at least 50 missed games.
Acuña hasn't just been one of the best hitters in baseball this month; he's reminded everyone he's one of the sport's biggest draws whenever he's healthy. Which raises the obvious question: Will the Atlanta Braves sign their franchise slugger long-term?
There are a few layers to that. Acuña is in the final guaranteed year of an eight-year, $100 million extension, with two club options for 2027 and 2028 that the Braves will undoubtedly exercise. But according to multiple analysts, a long-term deal getting done before he reaches free agency is far from certain, given both his injury history and general manager Alex Anthopoulos's general reluctance to make massive long-term commitments.
That hesitation has precedent. Anthopoulos and the Braves have let franchise cornerstones like Freddie Freeman, Dansby Swanson and Max Fried all walk away in recent offseasons, betting he could find comparable production for less money elsewhere — and largely, that bet has paid off, even if the solutions haven't all come from the same place.
Matt Olson, acquired via trade, has effectively replaced Freeman's production at first base, and a wave of young, club-controlled arms developed within Atlanta's own system has kept the rotation competitive behind Chris Sale even as Fried starred elsewhere.
Shortstop is a bit different. Mauricio Dubón has helped the Braves finally find a viable shortstop, whch they had been looking for since Swanson's departure. But even he's more of a stopgap in 2026 than the long-term answer, with genuine farm system options like Tatie Southisene, John Gil and Alex Lodise all competing to be the shortstop of the future.
Say what you want about those moves, but collectively, they worked. Freeman, Fried and Swanson are all great, even star-caliber players. Freeman is a future Hall of Famer. Yet, Atlanta found a way to replace each of them anyway.
Acuña is a different animal entirely. He's not just a star; he's a superstar, a sparkplug, the conduit every other piece of this offense runs through. We've already seen how much the Braves struggle with outfield-by-committee whenever he or Michael Harris II has to miss time.
Compare that to shortstop, where prospects like Southisene, Gil and Lodise are all competing to be the long-term answer, or even the rotation, where the system has produced options — the outfield simply doesn't have that same kind of depth waiting in the wings anymore. That makes keeping Acuña in Atlanta feel less like a preference and more like a necessity.
Acuña has an MVP under his belt, which he won after an unprecedented 40/70 season. Sure, they've let an MVP walk before, Freeman, an replaced him with an All-Star in Olson. Good luck doing that again and with even better ballplayer like Acuña.
That's why Acuña could be an exception to Anthopoulos's usual approach, and why he'll ultimately open up the checkbook before Acuña reaches unrestricted free agency in 2029.
There's also the competitive angle to consider. If Anthopoulos were to let Acuña walk, which teams are aggressive enough spenders to actually land him? The Mets, Phillies and Dodgers top that list — and even with Anthopoulos's track record of letting players leave for greener pastures, it's hard to imagine him handing one of the game's most electric superstars to one of Atlanta's three most bitter rivals.
The Braves face plenty of tough contract questions, but this one might be the most straightforward. Time will tell, but I think Anthopoulos will ultimately make the right call.

item.title: [sports.yahoo.com] Braves’ Chris Sale Sends 3-Word Red Sox Message After Brutal Trade
item.dc:creator: Peter Chawaga; Contributor
item.description: The Atlanta Braves and Boston Red Sox are both preparing for postseason pushes, but their paths since one of the most consequential recent trades between the clubs could hardly look more different. Boston traded likely Hall of Famer Chris Sale to Atlanta before the 2024 season, receiving Vaughn Grissom in return while also sending $17 million to the Braves. At the time, Sale was coming off several injury-plagued seasons, having made just 31 starts from 2020 through 2023. The Red Sox appeared to
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves and Boston Red Sox are both preparing for postseason pushes, but their paths since one of the most consequential recent trades between the clubs could hardly look more different.
Boston traded likely Hall of Famer Chris Sale to Atlanta before the 2024 season, receiving Vaughn Grissom in return while also sending $17 million to the Braves. At the time, Sale was coming off several injury-plagued seasons, having made just 31 starts from 2020 through 2023. The Red Sox appeared to be moving on from an accomplished pitcher whose best days might have been behind him.
Instead, Sale has experienced a remarkable career revival in Atlanta, leaving many Red Sox fans embittered by the decision to part ways with him.
"Sale entered the 2024 season thinking it would be the last of his career, and he exited it with his first career Cy Young Award," Mark Bowman wrote for MLB.com. "Injuries had limited him to 151 innings from 2021-23. But he has continued to get better through each of his first three seasons with Atlanta."
Now, with both teams looking toward October, Sale has offered a revealing response about that fateful transaction.
Atlanta Braves' Chris Sale Offers 3-Word Response On Boston Red Sox Trade
During a recent interview with Baseball Is Dead, Sale was asked whether he believed he would have enjoyed the same career renaissance if he had remained with the Red Sox.
"I don't know," Sale responded several tines. "I get traded and I found a new trainer… And I really felt like that helped me a lot with my health."
While Red Sox fans will never know if Sale would have been able to deliver a similar 2024 campaign in Boston, the Braves' superstar did go on to suggest he was only able to maintain his health thanks to a new training program away from Red Sox facilities.
Atlanta Braves' Star Chris Sale Sends Message On Health Issues With Boston Red Sox
The results since the trade have been striking. Sale posted an 18-3 record with a 2.38 ERA and 225 strikeouts in 2024, winning his first Cy Young Award at age 35.
His comments also suggest that the move represented more than simply changing uniforms.
"If I had stayed in Boston, would it have been the same? I don't know," Sale added. "It's hard to tell, but because of the trade, I've found someone and got into some places and did some things that really helped me be healthy again."
That distinction matters when assessing the deal. Sale's Boston tenure included a World Series championship and some dominance, but injuries dramatically limited his availability late in his Red Sox career. Boston traded him after he made only 20 starts in 2023.
Atlanta, meanwhile, has received the version of Sale that Boston hoped it could keep healthy. In 2026, he earned his 10th All-Star selection and continued adding to his impressive Braves resume.
The trade will inevitably remain a fascinating what-if for both fan bases, particularly as Sale and the Braves enter another postseason chase.
This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal warmed up for the postseason with seven dominant innings, Teoscar Hernandez and Andy Pages provided all the offense with home runs, and the Los Angeles Dodgers opened a three-game road series against the San Francisco Giants with a 2-0 victory Friday night.
Making his 10th start since joining the two-time defending champs at the trade deadline, Skubal (12-7) allowed just three singles and no walks in winning his fourth consecutive start. He struck out 10, reaching double figures for the fourth time this season.
The Dodgers (98-62), who have clinched the National League West title and the No. 2 seed in the upcoming NL playoffs, provided the left-hander all the run support he would need in the second inning against Giants starter Yunior Marte (0-2).
After the right-hander had escaped a two-on, two-out jam in the first, Hernandez launched the rookie’s first pitch of the second inning into the left field bleachers for his 16th home run of the season.
After Max Muncy lined out to right field Pages followed Hernandez’s flight pattern, reaching the left field seats with his 22nd home run of the year and a 2-0 lead.
In his third big-league start, Marte was able to finish five innings with no further damage, leaving after allowing just the two runs and six hits. He walked one and struck out four.
Giants relievers Sam Hentges, Joel Kuhnel, Dylan Smith and Tristan Beck kept the hosts close with an inning of shutout relief apiece.
But the San Francisco offense couldn’t fire against Skubal and relievers Roki Sasaki and Tanner Scott. The trio combined to retire 20 of the final 21 Giants batters after Scott Bandura’s one-out single in the third.
Scott was credited with his 24th save after throwing a two-strikeout ninth, ending LA’s two-game losing streak.
The shutout win was the Dodgers’ 14th of the season and the first for Skubal since moving west from Detroit.
Will Smith had three hits and Pages a pair for the Dodgers, who out-hit the Giants 7-3. Every hit in the game other than the home runs was a single.
Victor Bericoto, who was thrown out trying to stretch a single into a double in the first inning, Bandura in the third and Bo Davidson in the seventh got the only hits for the Giants (65-95), who lost their third straight overall and their sixth in a row to the rival Dodgers.
–Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
SAN DIEGO (AP) — Nolan Arenado hit one of Arizona's three home runs and Geraldo Perdomo drove in four runs for the Diamondbacks, who beat San Diego 11-4 on Friday night to remain alive for the National League's final wild-card spot.
Lars Nootbar and Jordan Lawlar also homered in the victory, which kept San Diego from clinching the No. 4 seed and home-field advantage in the wild-card round next week.
Brandon Pfaadt (8-3) beat the Padres for the third time this season with 7 2/3 innings. He allowed four runs and nine hits, struck out seven and walked two.
San Diego and Chicago clinched wild-card berths on Thursday, leaving Philadelphia and Arizona to fight it out for the third spot. Arizona is one game behind the Phillies with two to play.
The Diamondbacks and Padres knew that the Cubs had been swept by Boston in a doubleheader and that Philadelphia had lost to Tampa Bay.
The Padres then just needed to beat the Diamondbacks to clinch the No. 4 seed.
But Casey Mize (6-10) allowed the three home runs to jeopardize his spot on the wild-card roster and the Padres were booed a few times a night after clinching their club-record third straight postseason berth with a 4-2 win at the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Nootbar drove Mize's first pitch into the home-run porch in the right-field corner. Perdomo hit an RBI triple and Corbin Carroll a sacrifice fly to make it 3-0.
Lawlar homered to right field with one out in the second. Arenado drove a two-run shot off the third level of the Western Metal Supply Co. brick warehouse in the left-field corner with two outs in the third, his 30th, for a 6-2 lead.
Gabriel Moreno hit an RBI single in the fourth and, after Kyle Hart walked the bases loaded in the sixth, Perdomo cleared them with a double that bounced off the glove of retreating center fielder Jackson Merrill and then off the padded fence.
Padres center fielder Jase Bowen robbed Perdomo of a home run to end the eighth and then stole one from Tim Tawa to end the ninth.
Up next
Arizona was pondering its options for Saturday night after placing RHP Corbin Burnes on the injured list with shoulder inflammation. The Padres will go with RHP Walker Buehler (9-6, 4.56 ERA).

item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Tarik Skubal was showing no signs of slowing down in what was shaping up to be his most dominant start as a Dodger. But after throwing seven scoreless innings on 75 pitches, the southpaw was shaking hands and receiving hugs in the visitors' dugout at Oracle Park.
Skubal struck out 10, gave up just three hits and faced two batters over the minimum in his final regular-season start on Friday night.
His pitch count was in such a good spot that he could have made a bid for the second "Maddux" of his career. But when the bottom of the eighth inning came around, Skubal remained in the dugout and Roki Sasaki relieved him on the mound.
“That was the best we’ve seen," manager Dave Roberts said. "He was on a mission tonight. You could see it. Everything was working. He just went after those guys and did a fantastic job."
While Roberts has maintained that the Dodgers won't approach their final games of the season differently with the No. 2 postseason seed locked in, the 2-0 win over the Giants was an example of how having nothing left to play for changes the calculus of in-game decisions.
With five days off before the NL Division Series begins on Oct. 3 at Dodger Stadium, Roberts isn't necessarily looking to use this weekend for load management. But these final games are the Dodgers' last opportunity to try out players in their postseason roles in a lower-stakes environment.
Had this game taken place a week ago, Skubal may have stayed in to finish off his gem. But the Dodgers had already planned on having Sasaki pitch on Friday, and with only two additional games remaining for him to prepare for his postseason bullpen role, they opted not to deviate from that plan.
Sasaki got his work in, tossing a 1-2-3 eighth inning with two strikeouts in his second appearance back from the injured list. Tanner Scott closed out the victory, the Dodgers' 98th of the season -- which could be a hint at how both leverage arms will be used in the postseason.
"It’s better to have as many guys as you have confidence in in leverage," Roberts said. "So it just allows us to deploy guys whenever we need to."
For much of Skubal's two months as a Dodger, both he and the team maintained that they had not seen him at his best on the mound. Not only was Friday his best performance yet with L.A., but it came against a team that had frustrated him just six days earlier.
Last Saturday, Skubal lasted only five innings while allowing four runs against the Giants at Dodger Stadium. He bemoaned his lack of fastball command, which he believed was the main factor behind the disappointing results.
Skubal didn't just have command of his fastball on Friday. He had command of everything, throwing 60 of his 75 pitches for strikes and going 21-for-23 in first-pitch strikes. He generated 21 whiffs on 43 swings (48.8%), including a season-high 12 on his fastball.
"I think it's the key to who I am. I think it makes me who I am," Skubal said. "I don't know how many pitches I threw tonight, but felt like there were only like 14 or 15 balls out of however many throws. … I'm not going to do that every time, but I think that just speaks to conviction and the pitch-calling."
Said Giants manager Tony Vitello: "He’s going to come right at you, so maybe we could have been a little more aggressive early. But the bottom line is, he was sharper than the other night [in L.A.], and maybe we weren’t as sharp."
While Skubal received minimal run support -- solo homers from Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages in the second inning -- he had no issues holding the line.
Along with Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, Skubal is part of the four-man gauntlet the Dodgers will run out in October. In his final tuneup, he looked postseason-ready, and then some.
"Once the months change and the playoffs start, nothing matters," Skubal said. "It's just about winning that game, and that's how I treat every single start. Because I'm just trying to put our team in a position to win a baseball game, and that won't change from today and whenever my next start is."

item.title: [New York Post] Tarik Skubal ‘not really satisfied’ yet despite dominating Giants in Dodgers’ playoff tune-up

item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO –– In his final tune-up of the regular season, Tarik Skubal looked like a well-oiled machine.
After looking good, but not often great, in his first couple months with the Dodgers, the team’s marquee trade deadline acquisition tapped back into his two-time Cy Young-winning form on Friday night, carving up the San Francisco Giants in a 2-0 win that could portend big things in the playoffs.
“That was the best we’ve seen,” manager Dave Roberts said. “He was on a mission tonight. You could see it. Everything was working … Incredibly good.”
During his scoreless seven-inning start, Skubal struck out 10 batters and allowed just three hits. He didn’t issue a walk. He hardly even looked stressed during an uber-efficient 75-pitch domination.
In his entire MLB career, the only time he posted a better stat line might have been in his lone complete-game shutout last year against the Cleveland Guardians.
“It’s just pitching aggressive and challenging them,” Skubal said. “Tough park to hit in. And the wind seemed like it was blowing in, kind of keeping fly balls in the yard tonight. So just challenge them and see how far they can hit it.”
The Dodgers, of course, didn’t need proof of such excellence from Skubal.
When they acquired him from the Tigers two months ago, they knew they had landed the one player available at this year’s deadline capable of significantly boosting their World Series odds.
Still, the left-hander’s acclimation process wasn’t exactly seamless.
He felt like he was being “a little too fine” at times, recording only one start without a walk in his first nine Dodgers outings. He didn’t have a scoreless performance until two weeks ago in Cincinnati, when he blanked the Reds over seven innings with nine strikeouts and only three hits allowed. And even then, he turned right back around and allowed four runs in five innings against the Giants his last time out –– showing visible frustration with himself before spending a few days earlier this week away from the team on the bereavement list.
“I’m not attacking the way I know how to attack,” he said. “My stuff’s too good to give a guy a free pass.”
Friday’s rematch at Oracle Park followed an entirely different script.
Skubal was handed a 2-0 lead in the second, after Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages hit a pair of home runs in a three-batter sequence (for Pages, it was his first long ball since returning from a fractured hand last week).
And from there, the 29-year-old Northern California native never looked back.
He pounded the Giants with a steady diet of fastballs (even hitting 100 mph at one point for only the third time this year) and changeups (commanding it better than he had for most of the last couple months) while also starting out with a first-pitch strike to 21 of his 23 batters.
“First-pitch strikes [are important],” Skubal said. “Today’s game gets very analytical. I think when I’m really good, it’s at the old-school stuff. Like getting ahead, winning your 1-1 counts, getting guys out in three or four pitches.”
Did Skubal think he “bullied” the Giants’ overmatched offense?
“I’m not going to use that word,” he joked. “That’ll make a pretty good headline if I say that.”
With Friday’s performance, Skubal finished his regular season with a 12-7 record and 2.72 ERA overall. Following his trade to the Dodgers, he went 5-2 and posted a 2.61 ERA in 10 starts, the last four of which were all winning decisions.
“Those numbers are great,” he said. “I think there’s just some things where I could be better. Today was a really good day. But I’ve also had some kind of poor performances … I think there’s always room for improvement. I’m not really satisfied with anything I’ve accomplished so far.”
The only caveat to Friday’s gem: The Giants are trotting out what is effectively a Triple-A lineup, as they limp to the end of a dismal 2026 season in which all of their big stars first struggled, then got hurt.
Still, there are worse ways to enter the playoffs than off the back of what was arguably his most complete start all season.
Friday, after all, was exactly what the Dodgers were envisioning when they traded for Skubal at the deadline.
They will be hoping it’s the start of more things to come in October.

item.content:encoded:
It didn't matter that Tarik Skubal's heater zipped across the middle of the plate, belt high to San Francisco Giants rookie Bo Davidson. The Dodgers' left-hander had been unhittable all inning, and the 100-mph fastball he reached back for to end the fourth was no exception.
It was just the third time Skubal had touched 100 mph all season, and Davidson waved at the pitch, falling to the same fate as his teammates before him, as Skubal struck out the side in order.
Skubal's final regular-season tuneup, in the Dodgers' 2-0 win on Friday, went swimmingly. In an efficient seven scoreless innings, Skubal threw just 75 pitches.
"When the shape's good, you're confident in your stuff over the zone," Skubal said. "And then, you're getting into leverage like I was able to, and you can kind of let it go. So that's kind of a product of all that."
The gem brought Skubal's regular-season ERA to 2.72, and 2.61 since the Dodgers (98-62) acquired him from the Detroit Tigers at the trade deadline.
"That was the best we've seen," manager Dave Roberts said. "He was on a mission tonight. You could see it. Everything was working. He just went after those guys and did a fantastic job. Pounded the zone."
At the time of the trade, his addition looked like a luxury for a team that already boasted one of the best rotations in the majors, assuming two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani would eventually return to the mound.
When he didn't, instead landing on the injured list for two weeks, Skubal's smooth transition turned what could have been a shock wave of a loss for the rotation into barely a tremor.
Even without Ohtani, the Dodgers' projected postseason rotation of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow is still drawing comparisons to the '90s Atlanta Braves.
Next, they'll test that association under postseason conditions. Skubal's outing Friday sent him into the first-round bye on a high note.
"I don't think it really matters," Skubal said. "I kind of treat every start the same. I'm going to try and go out there and put our team in a position to win, and that won't change in a regular season [game]. It's not like I needed to have a good one to be confident going into October. Once the months change and the playoffs start, nothing matters, it's just about winning that game, and that's how I treat every single start."
Even so, Skubal had highlighted fastball command as the main problem with his start last week, also against the Giants, when he gave up a season-high-tying four runs in five innings.
On Friday, he was the aggressor.
"It's an explosive fastball," Roberts said. "He stays behind it well, he hides it well. And then he's got the secondaries to go with it. So, tonight certainly was really dominant with the fastball, and ... could do whatever he wanted tonight."
Skubal only gave up three hits, all singles, one of which third baseman Max Muncy knocked down the line before the soft grounder could leave the infield in the seventh inning. Skubal retired 13 of the last 14 batters he faced.
In all, Skubal recorded 10 strikeouts, reaching double digits for the fourth time this season.
"Today's game gets very analytical," Skubal said. "I think when I'm really good at the old-school stuff, like getting ahead, winning your 1-1 counts, getting guys out in three or four pitches, they don't see me a lot. Our innings are pretty quick, gets our guys in the dugout. Doesn't allow them to get into rhythm and kind of see anything, so that's kind of how I assess most of my outings."
Roki Sasaki — continuing to log innings in relief in preparation for his postseason role — threw a perfect eighth. Tanner Scott retired the side in the ninth to record the save.
The Dodgers' offense came via the long ball. Teoscar Hernández continued his red-hot September with a solo home run in the second inning, his fifth homer in a month. Andy Pages followed two batters later with a home run, his first since coming off the injured list this week.
Read more: Swanson: Is he truly back? Shohei Ohtani showing signs he's regaining MVP form
This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times.

Bichette went 2-for-4 with an RBI double and a solo home run during the Mets' 7-6 loss to the Nationals on Friday.
Bichette tied things up at 2-2 with an RBI double in the third inning before adding a solo homer in the fifth. item.content:encoded:
The Seattle Mariners are playing for pride, considering that they are eliminated from MLB playoff contention. They dropped their first game against the Los Angeles Angels 4-6 on Thursday night. Before the first pitch of Game 2, some big news about Cal Raleigh has been announced.
On Friday night, the Mariners versus Angels game will be broadcast at 8:10 PM Mountain Time, 7:10 PM Pacific Time. Reid Detmers will take the mound for the Angels, and Bryce Miller will start for the Mariners.
Seattle Mariners News: Cal Raleigh News Before Game 2 Against The Los Angeles Angels
Before both teams take to the mound on Friday, September 25th, the team announced news regarding Raleigh.
"Mariners 9/25 R. Arozarena DH D. Canzone RF J. Rodríguez CF J. Naylor 1B M. Arroyo LF C. Young 2B J. Pereda C W. Wilson 3B L. Rivas SS B. Miller SP," Underdog MLB wrote about the Mariners lineup announcement.
The biggest change in this lineup is Raleigh coming out, with Jhonny Pereda coming in at catcher. Additionally, Weston Wilson and Michael Arroyo are coming in while Lazaro Montes and J.P. Crawford are being removed.
Raleigh has struggled at times during this season; however, the 29-year-old catcher still has 23 home runs this year.
Looking At Cal Raleigh & Jhonny Pereda
Raleigh has been with the Mariners for his entire six-year MLB career.
This year, he has recorded 79 hits, 15 doubles, 68 RBIs, and two stolen bases. However, Raleigh is putting up a measly .179 batting average, the worst of his young career.
Alternatively, Pereda has been having a solid year.
The 30-year-old catcher has only played 29 games this year. However, Pereda has recorded 25 hits, one double, eight RBIs, seven walks, and two home runs.
Raleigh is in the first year of a six-year, $105 million contract extension he signed in March 2025.
With this contract length still remaining, it's unlikely he will be moved in the offseason. More than likely, he will be on the Mariners team until his contract expires.
Mariners fans should hope he regains his form next year after a long offseason of training.
For now, they will likely flip-flop between Raleigh and Pereda for the remainder of the games.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Seattle Mariners Announce Sudden Cal Raleigh Decision During Angels Series appeared first on HEAVY.

item.content:encoded:
SAN DIEGO — Arizona right-hander Corbin Burnes was placed on the 15-day injured list on with shoulder inflammation on Friday, a day before he was to start for the Diamondbacks as they try to stay alive for the National League's final wild-card spot.
Burnes has made only three starts this season. He returned to the major leagues on Sept. 8 after a 15-month recovery from Tommy John surgery and had a 7.84 ERA with no decisions, eight strikeouts and four walks in 10 1/3 innings.
Arizona was considering its options for Saturday night, basing them in large part on how the Diamondbacks do Friday night. Arizona recalled right-hander Jose Cabrera from Triple-A Reno.
Chicago and San Diego have clinched wild-card spots.
With Philadelphia losing 2-0 to Tampa Bay, the Diamondbacks were 1 1/2 games back for the final spot heading into their game at San Diego. Their magic number for elimination was two.
The Diamondbacks took an early 6-2 lead on home runs by Nolan Arenado, Lars Nootbar and Jordan Lawlar.

item.content:encoded:
Ortiz was removed from Friday's game against the Cardinals with an apparent injury, Jack Stern of BrewerFanatic.com reports.
Ortiz appeared to tweak something while legging out an infield single in the second inning and was eventually taken out of the game in the eighth. The Brewers will likely provide an update on his status after the game once they take a closer look at him, but he could sit out the team's final two regular-season games as a precaution to keep him as healthy as possible for the postseason.

item.content:encoded:
Sep 25, 2026, 9:16 PM ET
Seattle Mariners relief pitcher Andres Munoz (knee) was placed on the 15-day Injured List on Friday, Ryan Divish reports. Munoz hasn't pitched since Sunday, and now goes to the shelf due to right knee inflammation. His inconsistent 2026 season will now come to an end with a few games left in the regular season. He'll finish the season with a 4.24 ERA, 1.22 WHIP, and an 89/24 K/BB ratio with 28 saves across 57.2 innings of work. The expectation is that Jose A. Ferrer and Seranthony Dominguez will work in save situations over the final few days of the regular season. Fantasy managers should expect Munoz to be back in the closer role and fully healthy for the start of next season.--Andy Webb
Source: Ryan Divish
More Recent News
Xavier Edwards Still Out for Marlins


Keith Hernandez




Sep 25, 2026, 6:07 PM ET
Miami Marlins middle infielder Xavier Edwards (thumb) remains out of the starting nine for Friday's series opener at home against the division-rival Atlanta Braves, per MLB.com. Jared Serna will make another start at second base for the Fish and will hit in the nine-hole against Braves left-hander Ray Kerr. This will be Edwards' fifth straight missed game after he aggravated a left-thumb injury last Saturday against the San Diego Padres. The Marlins have not rushed the 27-year-old back after being eliminated from playoff contention. At this point, he only has two more chances to return before the end of the regular season on Saturday and Sunday against Atlanta. The switch-hitting middle infielder was having a second straight solid season for the Fish this year, slashing .280/.360/.371 with a .730 OPS, a career-high six home runs, 52 RBI, 21 stolen bases, and 61 runs scored across 142 games and 595 plate appearances. You are not going to get any power from Edwards, but he remains useful for his speed and contact-oriented approach at the dish in fantasy leagues.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Luis Arraez Out on Friday, Report "Not a Great One"


Keith Hernandez




Sep 25, 2026, 6:01 PM ET
Philadelphia Phillies infielder Luis Arraez (ankle) is out of the team's starting lineup on Friday against the visiting Tampa Bay Rays, and the report on his ankle injury from Thursday night is "not a great one," interim manager Don Mattingly told Scott Lauber of The Philadelphia Inquirer. Mattingly did not give a grade on the sprain, and the Phillies have not decided on an injured-list placement, which would take Arraez out until at least Oct. 5, or around Game 3 of the divisional round. X-rays on Arraez's left ankle came back negative on Thursday night, but his sprained ankle is still stiff and sore, which is why he will not play on Friday. Bryson Stott is at second base and batting fifth on Friday, with Edmundo Sosa at third base and hitting ninth against Rays right-hander Freddy Peralta. The Phillies would obviously love to avoid putting the 29-year-old All-Star on the IL, but if he cannot play at all this weekend, they might have no choice. The four-time All-Star and three-time batting champion has hit only .278 (49-for-176) in his 46 games with the Phillies this year after being traded from the San Francisco Giants in early August, but he is still the league's leading hitter at .310 overall. Not having Arraez available next week for the start of the playoffs (if the Phillies qualify) would be a big loss for Philadelphia.--Keith Hernandez

item.content:encoded:
Mariners place closer Andrés Muñoz on IL, recall reliever
Troy Taylor was called up from the minors to replace the two-time All-Star.
(Olivia Vanni/Getty Images)
The Seattle Mariners placed closer Andrés Muñoz on the 15-day injured list with right knee inflammation Friday.
Right-hander Troy Taylor was recalled from Triple-A Tacoma in a corresponding move.
Muñoz was removed from his outing Sunday against the Colorado Rockies with the knee issue after facing three batters, which included allowing a home run and a walk.
General manager Justin Hollander on Tuesday said Muñoz could be available in a save situation that night as Seattle was opening a two-game series against the Houston Astros that held playoff implications. But the Mariners fell 7-0 Tuesday, and Muñoz didn’t pitch Wednesday during a 7-6 win over Houston in 10 innings that provided multiple high-leverage spots the right-hander could have been used in.
The IL stint will end Muñoz’s season since Seattle had just three games left to play entering Friday. An up-and-down year resulted in the two-time All-Star posting a 5-6 record, 4.24 ERA and 1.22 WHIP with 89 strikeouts to 24 walks in 57 1/3 innings over 61 appearances. Muñoz was 28 of 38 save opportunities this year. His 10 blown saves are tied with Detroit’s Kyle Finnegan for the most in baseball.
Taylor is back for his second stint in the majors this year, though he hasn’t pitched in a big-league game since May of last season. In 54 appearances with Tacoma this year, he had a 1-2 record, 5.05 ERA, 1.75 WHIP and 65 strikeouts to 37 walks over 57 innings.
The Mariners continue their series against the Angels at 7:10 p.m. on Friday. Radio coverage on Seattle Sports 710 AM and the Seattle Sports app starts with the pregame show at 6 p.m.

item.title: [mlb.com] Riley started week with toothache -- then started to find his swing
item.dc:creator: Mark Bowman

item.content:encoded:
MIAMI -- Now that Austin Riley has created some encouragement by homering a couple times this week, should the Braves’ third baseman begin every week of the postseason by undergoing an emergency root canal?
“No, I wouldn’t wish that on my worst enemy,” Riley said.
Riley’s bid to homer in a third straight game proved unsuccessful in a 3-0 loss to the Marlins on Friday night at loanDepot park. But having homered against the Reds on Wednesday and Thursday, it’s safe to say this week has progressed much better than it started.
An intense toothache woke Riley around 5 a.m. CT on Sunday in his Houston hotel. The Braves arranged for him to visit a dentist, who was unable to do the root canal because of staffing issues. After returning to Daikin Park, the two-time All-Star felt incredible pain after biting into a sandwich.
Braves head athletic trainer George Poulis then arranged for Riley to visit another dentist, who completed the root canal and sent the slugger back to the stadium in time to be with his teammates as they celebrated clinching the NL East.
“My face was half numb, but it was all good,” Riley said.
Unfortunately for Riley, he hasn’t been numb to the frustration he has felt while producing career lows in both batting average (.222) and OPS (.662). He’s also set a franchise single-season record with a career-high 197 strikeouts, two of which were registered as Eury Pérez dazzled the Braves with a one-hit shutout on Friday.
With four homers in his past 18 games, Riley needs to go deep just one time in the regular season’s final two games to secure a 20-homer season. That’s a satisfying number when you consider he hit just nine in the season’s first 95 games. But this is a guy who tallied three straight 30-homer seasons from 2021-23.
“I don’t even look at [the stats] anymore,” Riley said. “At this point, it’s about, ‘What can I do today, and what can I do going forward?’”
When the Braves begin the Wild Card Series on Tuesday at Truist Park, Riley will be working with a new slate. If he gets hot and helps Atlanta advance deep into the postseason, he can distance himself from what he has done over the past six months.
“Austin's great,” Braves manager Walt Weiss said. “You never know if he's had an MVP season or if he's struggling. He’s the same guy. I know, obviously, he's been working really hard all year to try to turn things around, and I think he's trending the right way.”
Riley has been far more productive during the season’s second half. But the strikeout rate has been more alarming.
Pre-All-Star break: .207 BA, 9 HRs (38.1 At-bats per homer), .618 OPS, 29.4% strikeout rate
Post-AS break: .247 BA, 10 HRs (21.5 AB/HR), .734 OPS, 35.6% K rate
September: .222 BA, 4 HRs (18 AB/HR) .695 OPS, 32.9% K rate
Burdened by an abundance of video analysis and analytical data, Riley has been looking to simplify both his swing and his mindset. He knows he has looked robotic with many of his swings this year. But he feels good about an adjustment he made last weekend, when he noticed his right shoulder seemed to be tense and pointed inward with his stance.
Riley has spent the past few games focused on keeping that shoulder loose, with the hope he reduces the frequency with which he has pushed the bat through the zone or flipped the bat through the zone. His aim has been to make his swing look more natural.
“I definitely think this is the most confident I’ve been in a while with some of [the] cues and with some of the swings I’ve taken,” Riley said.

item.content:encoded:
Shota Imanaga doesn’t need anyone else’s help celebrating.
The Cubs pitcher went viral after repeatedly blasting himself in the face with beer during the team’s wild clubhouse celebration after clinching a spot in the postseason Thursday.
Naturally, Imanaga had an explanation for the madness.
“This is Japanese style,” Imanaga said while holding a bottle in each hand. “Japanese misogi.”
Imanaga then turned both bottles toward himself and sprayed the beer directly onto his head and face, bobbing up and down into the streams as his teammates laughed around him.
“Self-service!” Imanaga said.
The Cubs leaned into the moment themselves, posting the video on social media captioned: “Who needs bottle service when you have self-service?”
During an interview with Marquee Sports Network’s Taylor McGregor amid the clubhouse celebration, Imanaga was showered with champagne by his teammates.
His response?
“Yummy!”
Chicago officially punched its postseason ticket with a 2-1 victory over the Marlins at Wrigley Field, securing a playoff berth for the second consecutive season.
Seiya Suzuki tied the game with his 26th home run of the season in the fifth inning before Nico Hoerner drove home Ian Happ for the eventual winning run in the sixth.
Pete Crow-Armstrong also stole his 40th base of the season in the victory, giving him 40 home runs and 40 stolen bases and making him just the seventh player in MLB history to accomplish the feat.
Imanaga has played his part in getting Chicago back to the playoffs for the second consecutive season.
The 33-year-old left-hander went 11-10 with a 3.74 ERA while remaining a fixture in Chicago’s starting rotation throughout the season.
He also recorded 171 strikeouts in 173 ⅓ innings pitched in 2026.
Last year, the Cubs went 92-70 and took care of the Padres in the wild-card round before falling to the Brewers in five games in the NLDS.
Imanaga, who was an All-Star two seasons ago, turned 33 earlier this month and has a career 3.44 ERA and a 35-21 record.

item.content:encoded:
On Friday, the New York Yankees will open up a series with the Baltimore Orioles in the Bronx.
They will play a doubleheader.
The Yankees wrote (via X) on Thursday: “Saturday’s Yankees-Orioles game (Saturday, September 26) has been rescheduled due to the forecast of sustained inclement weather and will be made up tomorrow, Friday, September 25, as the first game of a single-admission doubleheader, which will begin at 4:05 p.m.”
UPDATE: The Yankees lost the first game 10-2.
New York Yankees Make Bellinger Change
The Yankees are coming off a 6-4 win over the Tampa Bay Rays on Thursday.
Cody Bellinger had no hits in four at-bats.
For Friday’s first game, the Yankees have announced their starting lineup.
Underdog MLB wrote: “Yankees Game 1 9/25 P. Goldschmidt 1B B. Rice DH H. Ramos LF A. Rosario RF G. Lombard Jr. SS S. Jones CF A. Volpe 3B A. Sánchez C J. Caballero 2B B. Beck SP”
Bellinger has been removed from the lineup on Friday.
The move is likely just for rest.
Right now, Bellinger is batting .266 with 131 hits, 17 home runs, 73 RBIs, 73 runs and 12 stolen bases in 131 games.
Bellinger is in the middle of his second year with the Yankees.
He has also spent time with the Los Angeles Dodgers and Chicago Cubs over 10 total seasons at the MLB level.
The three-time All-Star is a former MVP and World Series Champion.
Looking At The Yankees On Friday
The Yankees have already clinched a spot in the 2026 MLB playoffs.
They are the second-place team in the American League East with a 92-67 record in 159 games.
The Yankees wrote (via X): “Today’s CC Sabathia Ceremony will begin at 3:15 pm. Derek Jeter, Andy Pettitte, Dellin Betances, and Chris Young are set to join @CC_Sabathia as we honor his career and legacy. All @yankeestadium gates will open to fans at 2:30 pm, at which time distribution will begin for the September 25 scheduled promotional item (Josh Hart Yankees Bobblehead presented by Delta Air Lines for the 1st 18,000 Guests in attendance).”

item.content:encoded:
Las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol (MLB, por sus siglas en inglés) revelaron las 20 camisetas de peloteros más vendidas de la temporada 2026.
En la lista figura un solo pelotero venezolano: Ronald Acuña Jr., de los Bravos de Atlanta, quien ocupa la cuarta posición. En 2025, Acuña Jr. también figuró en este listado, pero en el puesto 11.
La publicación, difundida por la MLB en su cuenta de Instagram, reveló que el japonés Shohei Ohtani, de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, encabeza la lista de las camisetas más vendidas.
En cuanto a los equipos, los Dodgers de Los Ángeles son los que cuentan con más jugadores en la lista, con cuatro: Ohtani, Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts y Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
¿Quiénes son los 20 peloteros con las camisetas más vendidas en 2026?
De acuerdo con la lista difundida por la MLB, estas son las 20 camisetas más vendidas de la temporada 2026:
- Shohei Ohtani, Dodgers de Los Ángeles.
- Aaron Judge, Yankees de Nueva York.
- Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cachorros de Chicago.
- Ronald Acuña Jr., Bravos de Atlanta.
- Fernando Tatis Jr., Padres de San Diego.
- Freddie Freeman, Dodgers de Los Ángeles.
- Bryce Harper, Filis de Filadelfia.
- Mookie Betts, Dodgers de Los Ángeles.
- Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers de Los Ángeles.
- Juan Soto, Mets de Nueva York.
- Corey Seager, Texas Rangers.
- Vladimir Guerrero Jr., Toronto Blue Jays.
- Adley Rutschman, Medias Rojas de Boston.
- Kyle Schwarber, Filis de Filadelfia.
- Paul Skenes, Piratas de Pittsburgh.
- Cal Raleigh, Marineros de Seattle.
- Elly De La Cruz, Rojos de Cincinnati.
- Jackson Merrill, Padres de San Diego.
- Nolan Arenado, Arizona Diamondbacks.
- Munetaka Murakami, Chicago White Sox.
Shohei Ohtani encabeza por cuarto año consecutivo
El japonés Shohei Ohtani, de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, volvió a ser el jugador con la camiseta más vendida de las Grandes Ligas, una posición que ocupa por cuarto año consecutivo.
Ohtani se convirtió así en el primer jugador en encadenar cuatro temporadas como líder en ventas de camisetas desde que MLB comenzó a registrar este dato en 2010, reseñó la agencia de noticias EFE este viernes 25 de septiembre.
Desde 2023, los aficionados han comprado la camiseta Nike de Ohtani más que cualquier otra en Estados Unidos, Japón y el resto del mundo, consolidando al jugador japonés como la figura con mayor demanda comercial entre los peloteros de las Grandes Ligas.
El listado, elaborado a partir de las ventas de camisetas Nike realizadas a través de Fanatics, incluido MLBShop.com, desde el Día Inaugural de la temporada 2026, sitúa al capitán de los Yankees de Nueva York, Aaron Judge, en el segundo puesto y al jardinero de los Cachorros de Chicago Pete Crow-Armstrong en el tercero.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Alonso hits two more HRs in 10-2 Orioles win over Yanks

item.content:encoded:
This just in, ladies and gentlemen: Pete Alonso is really good at baseball.
The Most Valuable Oriole continued to be the best thing to happen to this franchise in a long time, adding two more homers to his league-leading total in a 10-2 blowout win to open a doubleheader against the Yankees.
Whatever other things have gone wrong for the Orioles this year — and oh boy, are there many — Pete Alonso has been worth the price of admission all by himself. Tonight, even in a game that had no meaning for either team, he proved why.
Alonso stepped to the plate with a man aboard in the third against Yankees starter Brendan Beck, who'd begun the game with two scoreless innings. Pete put an end to that real quick. He drove a 407-foot dinger into the left-field seats, his 42nd of the year. At that point, Alonso's last seven hits had all been dingers. Did I mention this guy is good at baseball?
The Orioles turned the game into a laugher in the fourth even without Pete being prominently involved (though he did get a single). The O's loaded the bases with nobody out for the soft underbelly of the lineup, including Christian Franklin and Carlos Narváez, who entered the game with a combined zero RBIs in 132 plate appearances with the Orioles. That's Caleb Joseph territory right there. Franklin managed to get off the schneid with a sharp single to right, collecting his first major league RBI, but Narváez remained in his drought by hitting into a force at the plate.
It shouldn't be that hard to get one measly RBI, Carlos. Just watch as Dylan Beavers gets four of them in one at-bat! The O's right fielder jumped on a hanging curveball from Beck and clobbered it into the right-field seats for his first career grand slam. Beavers! With one mighty swing, the Orioles had an insurmountable 7-0 lead.
The Birds' victory was all but assured, but that doesn't mean they couldn't have some more fun along the way. In the top of the sixth, Jeremiah Jackson lofted a fly ball to deep center field. Spencer Jones loped back at an ambling pace, as if he had the ball tracked all the way, but when he reached up to make the catch, it glanced off his glove and deflected to the wall. The ball trickled along the warning track for so long that Jackson just kept circling the bases, and by the time the Yankees got the ball into the infield, Jackson had slid in safely with an inside-the-park home run.
Look at the wheels on Jeremiah! If you'd told me that the Orioles would have two inside-the-parkers this season and they'd be hit by Coby Mayo and Jeremiah Jackson, I'm not sure I would've believed you. This has been a strange season, occasionally in good ways.
You know what's not strange? Pete Alonso being awesome. It's just what he does, and always has. Alonso led off the seventh against reliever Yerry de los Santos and absolutely demolished a baseball. Holy smokes, was it tattooed, a mammoth blast the landed high into the left-field bleacher seats.
Pete, that baseball had a family! The blast was his second of the game and AL-leading 43rd of the year, and extended his AL-leading RBI count to 112. In all likelihood, Pete is going to take two of the three Triple Crown categories. He won't win AL MVP, and I'm not saying he should, but…is there any player in the American League who's really that much better than him? I'd put him in my top five for sure.
This game was all Orioles, but if there was one disappointing aspect, it's that Trevor Rogers didn't get the chance to earn the win in what may well have been his final start as an Oriole. Rogers pitched brilliantly tonight as always, but the Orioles, in an apparently pre-planned move, removed him from the game after four innings and 55 pitches.
I mean…why? Rogers was showing no signs of fatigue. He mowed down the Yankees in the first four frames, throwing 41 strikes and just 14 balls. He allowed only one run, on an Amed Rosario RBI single in the fourth, and the O's had a comfortable six-run lead when he left. Was his arm really going to fall off if he threw more than 55 pitches in his final start of the season?
I will grant that he'd already thrown a career-high 169.2 innings this season, and perhaps the Orioles saw no reason to push him in a meaningless game, but I would've let him at least pitch one more inning to get a W next to his name. Mostly I just don't want to accept that this might've been the last time we see Rogers in an Orioles uniform.
The Orioles hit double digits in runs on Gunnar Henderson's RBI single in the eighth that deflected off the second baseman, and the bullpen took it from there. Albert Suárez, now in his sixth stint with the Orioles this year, did his usual quality work in long relief. He tossed four scoreless innings and struck out five, even despite a nosebleed that afflicted him in the eighth. Suárez has been an unsung hero of the O's bullpen, constantly eating up innings without complaint even when he knows he'll probably get DFA'd the next day, then inevitably returning to the roster to do it all over again.
Alex Hoppe's ninth inning was a mess — 22 pitches, two walks, and a run — but a nine-run lead gives you plenty of wiggle room, and he eventually finished it with a called strikeout of Ben Rice. Orioles win, 10-2. Not a bad way to start the weekend.

item.title: [Bozeman Daily Chronicle] Pete Alonso homers twice to take over AL lead as Orioles rout Yanks 10-2 in doubleheader opener
item.dc:creator: LARRY FLEISHER
item.description: NEW YORK (AP) — Pete Alonso homered twice to take over the American League lead with 43, including a 471-foot drive deep into the left field bleachers, and the Baltimore Orioles routed the New York Yankees 10-2 in a doubleheader opener on Friday. item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK (AP) — Pete Alonso homered twice to take over the American League lead with 43, including a 471-foot drive deep into the left field bleachers, and the Baltimore Orioles routed the New York Yankees 10-2 in a doubleheader opener on Friday.
Dylan Beavers had his first career grand slam in a five-run fourth and Jeremiah Jackson added an inside-the-park homer in the sixth.
Alonso hit rookie Brendan Beck's first-pitch slider in the third inning, becoming the first Oriole since Mark Trumbo in 2016 with seven straight hits that were homers.
Alonso singled in the fourth and three innings later hit a changeup at least halfway up the left field bleachers for a 9-1 lead, the fourth-longest homer in the major leagues this year.
Alonso moved out of a four-way tie for the AL home run lead. His 113 RBIs tied St. Louis' Alec Burleson for the big league high and the most by an Oriole since Chris Davis' 117 in 2015.
It was Alonso's 29th multi-homer game and third this year.
Beavers hit Baltimore's sixth grand slam this season, a drive into the right-field seats for a 7-0 lead.
Jackson added Baltimore’s second inside-the-park homer this year when he hit a fly ball that went over center fielder Spencer Jones’ glove at the warning track in front of New York’s bullpen. The ball caromed in front of the fence and Jackson crossed the plate ahead of right fielder Amed Rosario's throw.
Baltimore starter Trevor Rogers allowed one run and five hits in four innings. Albert Suárez (3-0) pitched four innings for the win.
Rosario had an RBI single for the Yankees, who honored Hall of Fame pitcher CC Sabathia by retiring his No. 52 and giving him a plaque in Monument Park in a pregame ceremony.
Anthony Volpe debuted at third base for the Yankees and had a double by Christian Encarnacion-Strand hit the bag go over his head in the ninth.
Beck (0-2) allowed seven runs and six hits in five innings.
Up Next
RHP Brandon Young (9-5, 3.62 ERA) starts for Baltimore in Game 2.

item.content:encoded:
【カブス3-4レッドソックス】ボストン／フェンウェイパーク、9月25日（日本時間26日）
レッドソックスは本拠地フェンウェイパークで行われたカブスとのダブルヘッダー第1試合に4-3で逆転勝利。ア・リーグの第5シードに入ることが確定し、ワイルドカードシリーズでは同地区の宿敵ヤンキースと対戦することになった。カブスの鈴木誠也は「2番・右翼」でスタメン出場し、初回の第1打席で四球を選んで先制のホームイン。しかし、その後はピッチャーゴロ、空振り三振、ショートゴロ、空振り三振と快音響かず、4打数無安打1四球で今季の打撃成績は打率.268、OPS.837となった。 レッドソックス先発のアレック・ガンボアは初回、1死から鈴木に四球を与え、2死後にタイロン・テイラーにレフトへのタイムリー二塁打を浴びて先制点を献上。二回は1死一、二塁の場面でミゲル・アマヤに2点タイムリー二塁打を浴び、2回4安打3失点で降板した。 しかし、ガンボア降板後、レッドソックス投手陣がカブス打線を封じた。2番手のジェイク・ベネットは3回2/3を3安打無失点に抑え、六回2死一塁の場面で登板した3番手のグレッグ・ワイサートも1回1/3を無失点。八回と九回は4番手のレイモンド・バーゴスが打者6人をパーフェクトに抑える好投を見せた。 レッドソックス打線は二回までカブス先発のクレイ・ホームズに無得点に抑えられていたが、三回にエラー絡みで1点を返すと、五回には1死二、三塁のチャンスを作り、ホームズを降板に追い込んだ。このあと、2番手のケイレブ・シールバーからアドリー・ラッチマンが2点タイムリーを放ち、3-3の同点に。リリーフ陣の奮闘に打線が応え、試合を振り出しに戻した。 2死満塁のピンチを切り抜けた直後の七回には勝ち越しのチャンスが到来。ロマン・アンソニーがライトへの三塁打を放ち、1死三塁となった。ここでコナー・ウォンがタイムリー二塁打を放ち、4-3と勝ち越しに成功。この1点を守り切って今季86勝目を挙げ、ア・リーグの第5シードを確定させた。 なお、カブスとレッドソックスは3連戦の最終戦を今日にスライドしてダブルヘッダーを開催し、明日がシーズン最終戦となる予定だったが、ボストンの天気が悪いため、明日の試合をレギュラーシーズン最終日となる27日（同28日）にスライドして開催地をレイズの本拠地であるトロピカーナフィールドに変更。確実に試合を消化できる日程が組まれることになった。

item.title: [MLB.com] Doc Emrick talks Pirates fandom, Paul Skenes and what makes Pittsburgh great
item.dc:creator: Jason Mackey

item.content:encoded:
DETROIT — Doc Emrick is most famous for his work as a Hall of Fame hockey broadcaster, but he’s always been a baseball fan at heart, especially when it comes to his beloved Pirates.
In fact, Emrick can pinpoint the exact day his Pirates fandom was solidified, which would surprise absolutely no one who’s ever listened to him call a hockey game.
The day was Aug. 9, 1959. The Pirates beat the Cubs at Wrigley Field in 10 innings, and Elroy Face earned the win. Emrick, who grew up in Fontaine, Ind. was there to witness it.
Initially intrigued by hearing Bob Prince call Pirates games on the radio, Emrick passed the point of no return when he saw the team win in person.
“I was hooked,” Emrick said Friday before the Pirates played the Tigers at Comerica Park. Emrick lives in St. Clair, Mich., about an hour north.
“I got to see three World Series championships, and the last guy who was on the mound when they won a World Series was Kent Tekulve. I’m proud to know him and have been around him down at fantasy camp.”
Emrick said it’s been about five years since he attended a Major League game but was thrilled to be around it live again. He watches every Pirates game back home and will join the SportsNet Pittsburgh broadcast alongside Greg Brown and John Wehner.
Predictably, Emrick was all smiles pregame while meeting with manager Don Kelly and saying hello to a few players, including noted hockey fan Spencer Horwitz.
“This is a special treat for me,” Emrick said. “The fact that I can see the Rock and Brownie and actually sit in with them [Friday], that’s special to me.”
Emrick participated in Pirates fantasy camp back in 2012 and encouraged anyone on the fence about doing it to take the plunge.
Starting with their Opening Day homers, Brandon Lowe and Ryan O’Hearn have been two of Emrick’s favorite players to watch this season, for how they seem to come through at important times.
On the pitching side, Emrick obviously enjoys watching Paul Skenes. But Mason Montgomery’s ascent this season has also been a pleasant surprise, leading Emrick to drop an obscure Ryne Duren (Google it) reference that’s very uniquely him.
“I like to see pitches thrown 100 or 101 miles per hour, because I could only imagine that when I was watching back in an earlier era,” Emrick said. “There was a pitcher for the New York Yankees that had Coke bottle glasses named Ryne Durne, and Yogi Berra felt that he probably pitched 90 miles an hour.
“Nobody wanted to bat against him, especially on a cold day. That was 90 [mph] and considered to be off the charts back then. The standard now is so much different.
“But to have confidence in a closer that comes out of the bullpen and you realize he’s probably got this thing, that’s really, really good. … I wish he could pitch every game. But you can’t expect that with that kind of velocity, for somebody to pitch every game.”
As for Skenes, Emrick enjoys how much attention he generates around MLB, basically as a point of pride for Pittsburgh. Emrick also isn’t upset that Skenes’ 2026 performance failed to meet previous standards set. In Emrick’s mind, that would’ve been darn near impossible.
“The first couple of years, the standard was so high,” Emrick said. “How is a human being going to rise above that for a third year in a row? Some of these recent outings that he’s had have been spectacular. It’s something to look forward to for the future.”
Emrick retired in October 2020 after 47 years of broadcasting hockey, which included the Stanley Cup Final 22 times. Given the Penguins’ success, Emrick was a regular presence in Pittsburgh and typically tried to work Pirates references into his hockey broadcasts.
There are also Pittsburgh ties with Emrick having taught speech and broadcasting at Geneva College, which basically makes him an honorary Yinzer.
Emrick said he appreciates Pittsburgh being so welcoming, along with the athletic success the city has enjoyed over the years.
“I’m just glad to be around you folks and travel into Pittsburgh now and then,” Emrick said. “I was thinking the other day, the city of Pittsburgh has had so many wonderful athletes in football, baseball and hockey. It’s easy to get spoiled. Not every city has that many that have been that prominent. And they tend to stay around there, don’t they?
“There’s not an edge to people in Pittsburgh. There’s just a general feeling that’s good.”

item.content:encoded:
Luis Arráez encendió las alarmas de Philadelphia durante la derrota 5-1 ante Milwaukee Brewers. El venezolano conectó un rodado en la sexta entrada y se torció el tobillo izquierdo cuando intentó evitar el toque del primera base Jake Bauers.
El infielder permaneció varios minutos en el terreno y necesitó ayuda del personal médico para caminar hasta el dugout. Los Phillies confirmaron posteriormente un esguince, aunque las radiografías descartaron una fractura.
- LEER MÁS: Los venezolanos que están marcando el cierre de MLB 2026
- LEER MÁS: Fernando Valenzuela: cómo la “Fernandomanía” transformó a la MLB
Todavía no existe una incapacidad oficial ni una fecha establecida para su regreso. El mánager interino Don Mattingly aseguró que espera poder utilizarlo nuevamente, pero su disponibilidad dependerá de la inflamación, el dolor y las evaluaciones realizadas durante el fin de semana.
El momento de la lesión aumenta la preocupación. Philadelphia posee marca de 87-72, ocupa el último comodín de la Liga Nacional y mantiene solamente dos juegos de ventaja sobre Arizona Diamondbacks cuando restan tres compromisos contra Tampa Bay Rays.
Suscríbete al Newsletter de Unanimo y recibe gratis las últimas noticias. Dale click aquí
Arráez se había convertido en una pieza importante desde su llegada procedente de San Francisco. En 45 partidos con los Phillies batea para .283, con dos jonrones, 21 carreras impulsadas y OPS de .690, generalmente como cuarto bate detrás de Bryce Harper.
Su ausencia también obligaría a modificar varias posiciones. Edmundo Sosa podría encargarse de la segunda base, mientras otra alternativa sería devolver a Harper a la inicial y reorganizar el outfield. Bryson Stott y Alec Bohm también podrían cambiar nuevamente de posición.
Luis Arráez went down in pain after running to 1st base on this play. He has left the game. pic.twitter.com/nbKPlGanAg
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) September 24, 2026
Philadelphia ya enfrenta otras dudas antes de octubre. Jesús Luzardo se encuentra en la lista de lesionados por una inflamación en el hombro izquierdo y el equipo acumula dos derrotas consecutivas, por lo que perder otro titular reduciría todavía más su margen de error.
Arráez no está descartado para los playoffs y las radiografías negativas representan la mejor noticia posible. Sin embargo, la Serie del Comodín comienza el martes y cualquier recuperación superior a cuatro días podría impedir que el venezolano participe desde el inicio.

item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers are coming off a series victory over the Philadelphia Phillies that they wrapped up Thursday with a 5-1 victory.
Now, they’re back home Friday night. And continue to inch closer to clinching the No. 1 overall seed in the National League as they begin their final series of the regular season against the St. Louis Cardinals.
On Friday night, Milwaukee will have right-handed pitcher Robert Gasser on the mound against Cardinals righty Michael McGreevy.
Ahead of the matchup, Brewers manager Pat Murphy made a notable change to the starting lineup involving veteran slugger Christian Yelich.
Brewers Announce Yelich Decision
After sitting Thursday in the series finale against Philly and making no pinch-hit appearances, Yelich is back in the order for Friday’s matchup.
Yelich will bat fifth in the order and serve as the team’s designated hitter, a usual spot for him this year as he’s entered more of a platoon role in his 14th MLB season.
Here’s the full Brewers lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Brewers 9/25 G. Mitchell CF B. Turang 2B W. Contreras C J. Bauers 1B C. Yelich DH J. Ortiz SS L. Lara RF S. Frelick LF D. Hamilton 3B R. Gasser SP.”
Brewers 9/25
G. Mitchell CF
B. Turang 2B
W. Contreras C
J. Bauers 1B
C. Yelich DH
J. Ortiz SS
L. Lara RF
S. Frelick LF
D. Hamilton 3B
R. Gasser SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 25, 2026
Looking at Yelich’s 2026 Season
While Yelich no longer plays every day or spends much time in the field. He remains an extremely productive player for a 100-win Brewers team that owns the best record in baseball.
Yelich has appeared in 115 games this season and logged 433 at-bats, recording 68 runs, 102 hits, 12 home runs, and 58 RBIs while hitting .236 and slugging .381 with a .695 OPS.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Red Sox Star Sonny Gray Gets Big Free Agency Prediction Just Before Playoffs
item.dc:creator: Matt Levine
item.description: The Boston Red Sox are getting ready for the final few games of the regular season, with the postseason starting up next week. Boston has clinched a playoff spot, and they will be a wild-card team this season. The Red Sox battled back from a very slow start to the season, putting together a massive rally in the middle of the year. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are getting ready for the final few games of the regular season, with the postseason starting up next week.
Boston has clinched a playoff spot, and they will be a wild-card team this season. The Red Sox battled back from a very slow start to the season, putting together a massive rally in the middle of the year.
The goal is to win a World Series title, and they seem to have a decent shot at getting it done. But while the players are focused on the play on the field, the front office also has its sights set on the upcoming offseason.
Even with the impending lockout likely coming to baseball, teams all over the league could try to maneuver rosters before it happens. For the Red Sox, they do have a key free agent hitting the market in ace Sonny Gray.
The veteran right-hander has been excellent for the Red Sox this year, firing a 2.79 ERA over 29 innings. Gray has helped establish the Red Sox rotation as one of the best in baseball, and he has been a major reason why the team has made the playoffs.
The right-hander has a mutual option for next season, but there has also been some retirement talk. However, given how strong of a year he has seen, the right-hander may postpone that idea, looking to land one last big contract.
Boston would surely want him back, but that all remains to be seen. But his free agency will be something to watch for the Red Sox and other potentially interested teams out there.
Sonny Gray Gets Major Free Agency Prediction
analyst Zach Buckley of Bleacher Report looked ahead to some of the bigger stars hitting the free-agent market this winter, predicting some of the outcomes. In this, Buckley has predicted that Gray will indeed return to the Red Sox following a strong season.
"It sounds like everything is on the table for the 36-year-old. Per Mass Live's Chris Cotillo, Gray could fetch a similar deal to the three-year, $75 million deal Nathan Eovaldi inked with the Texas Rangers two years back. But Cotillo also noted that Gray relayed in a recent interview with The Boston Globe he would retire "in a heartbeat" if his family indicated any desire for him to do so.
"Only Gray knows what he's thinking, and since he doesn't need to make a decision right now, it's very possible even if he isn't sure. If he wants to keep playing, though, he has clearly set himself up to strike it rich in free agency," Buckley wrote.
Should Red Sox Resign Sonny Gray?
Given how dominant Gray has been, the Red Sox should try to sign him to a new deal. Even if this would be just for another year or two, having Gray around would help Boston heading into next season.
Gray has seen a lot of success with the Red Sox, and the team is a contender, so the two sides may come together. But for now, the focus will be on trying to win the World Series, with free agency in the back of everyone's mind.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Red Sox Star Sonny Gray Gets Big Free Agency Prediction Just Before Playoffs appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [CBS Sports] Vladimir Guerrero Jr. apologizes for controversial comments about his $500 million contract
item.dc:creator: Dayn Perry
item.description: Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has apologized days after saying his $500 million contract extension rather than a reflection of his value moving forward. Guerrero Jr. on Friday, ahead of his team's season-ending home series against the Cincinnati Reds, issued the following statement, via MLB.com: "I want to tell everyone that I'm going to continue to keep working hard to make my contract a great one. … "I feel that the comments I made the other day is not what I really wan
item.content:encoded:
Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has apologized days after saying his $500 million contract extension rather than a reflection of his value moving forward.
Guerrero Jr. on Friday, ahead of his team's season-ending home series against the Cincinnati Reds, issued the following statement, via MLB.com:
"I want to tell everyone that I'm going to continue to keep working hard to make my contract a great one.
…
"I feel that the comments I made the other day is not what I really wanted to say. Everyone deserves an apology from me."
Guerrero Jr. said he regretted his comments and felt like he owed an apology to the fans and his teammates.
Vladdy starts his availability with a statement, through interpreter:
“The reason I'm here because I regret my comments the other day … I feel from my heart, my fans, my teammates, they needed an apology from me, and that's why I'm here for.”#BlueJays
Additionally, Guerrero Jr. said he decided to apologize after speaking with his father, Hall of Famer Vladimir Guerrero Sr.
The controversy stemmed from what the 27-year-old first baseman recently told Telemicro News, as translated by Héctor Gómez:
"The contract I got was based on what I did, not necessarily for what I'm going to do. I understand why the fans believe it's the other way around. Sometimes I think that way too, like 'oh they give me this money and I'm not doing enough', but you know I try my best and I'm working hard.
"The fans I know how they are, when you are doing great they are 100% behind you but when you are not at your best not everybody is behind you, almost nobody supports you. Those are my real fans, the ones that are supporting me all the time."
Guerrero Jr.'s original comments were ill-timed, as the reigning American League champion Blue Jays have been eliminated from playoff contention, and Guerrero Jr. himself has endured a highly disappointing season:
The above comes to an OPS+ of just 92, or a park-adjusted OPS that's 8% worse than the league average. Coming into 2026, he had a career OPS+ of 136. This season, Guerrero Jr. has hit just nine home runs and only one at home. He's slugged just .360, and his WAR has dropped from 4.6 a season ago to 1.3 in 2026. This decline in production has come in the first year of that $500 million extension, which will run through the 2039 season.
The only way Guerrero Jr. can truly put those struggles behind him is with a strong 2027, and his words on Friday suggest he's dedicated to making that happen.
The last-place Blue Jays enter the final weekend of the regular season with a record of 77-82, which means they've ensured a losing season for the second time in the last three years.
