item.content:encoded:
Brewers record their first 100-win season with victory over Phillies
The Milwaukee Brewers reached 100 wins for the first time, and Jackson Chourio hit his 25th homer to lift them to a 5-1 victory over Philadelphia on Thursday night that slowed the Phillies’ playoff push.
The Phillies needed a win to at least have a shot at clinching their fifth straight trip to the playoffs. They instead can try again to clinch for the third straight game on Friday against Tampa Bay.
Philadelphia played without NL batting leader Luis Arraez after he came off with a sprained left ankle after he tried to avoid a tag at first base.
Milwaukee reached one more milestone to go with its National League Central title and a first-round postseason bye. The Brewers are the first team this year to reach 100 wins and are trying to hold off the defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers for the No. 1 seed in the NL playoffs. Their previous high was 97 wins last year.
Brewers fans crowded the seats behind the dugout and held “100” signs as players left the field.
Bryce Harper tied the game 1-1 with an RBI single in the third.
Jake Bauers hit the tie-breaking single off José Alvarado (5-4) in the eighth inning, and Cooper Pratt and Joey Ortiz added run-scoring singles in the inning for a 4-1 lead. Chourio hit a solo shot in the ninth.
JoJo Romero (3-3) got the win and Antonio Senzatela earned his fourth save.
Phillies starter Andrew Painter had another terrific outing in a second-half rebound that should see him play a role in the postseason in the rotation or out of the bullpen. He allowed Sam Frelick’s RBI double in the second and finished with eight strikeouts and three walks in six innings.
The rookie right-hander was demoted to the minors in June after a 12-4 loss to Miami left him with eight losses in nine decisions and a 7.06 ERA. Since his July 31 recalled has a 3.65 ERA in 11 starts with 62 strikeouts to 23 walks.
Philadelphia got more good pitching news earlier in the day when All-Star lefty Jesús Luzardo said he has recovered enough from left shoulder inflammation that he should be able to pitch next week in the playoffs.
Up next
Milwaukee tunes up for the playoffs with a three-game homestand against St. Louis.

item.title: [mlb.com] Murphy sends message by pulling Contreras for not hustling on groundout
item.dc:creator: Adam McCalvy
item.description: PHILADELPHIA -- Even on the night his team became the first in the Majors in three years to win 100 games, Brewers manager Pat Murphy showed he still has the pedal to the metal. Murphy pulled one of his best players, All-Star catcher William Contreras, for a pinch-hitter in the eighth inning of Milwaukee’s 5-1 win over the Phillies on Thursday night at Citizens Bank Park. It proved to be the right move, because pinch-hitter Jackson Chourio responded by working a walk, stealing second base and sc
item.content:encoded:
PHILADELPHIA -- Even on the night his team became the first in the Majors in three years to win 100 games, Brewers manager Pat Murphy showed he still has the pedal to the metal.
Murphy pulled one of his best players, All-Star catcher William Contreras, for a pinch-hitter in the eighth inning of Milwaukee’s 5-1 win over the Phillies on Thursday night at Citizens Bank Park. It proved to be the right move, because pinch-hitter Jackson Chourio responded by working a walk, stealing second base and scoring the go-ahead run.
But it was also Murphy sending a message. Contreras had not run hard on a groundout to shortstop Trea Turner in the fifth inning. Turner bobbled the baseball, but still had plenty of time to throw to first for the inning-ending out in a tie game.
“I don’t know if he could have been safe or not,” Murphy said. “Everybody knows how much William does for our team, how hard he plays and how much he competes. But he’s also a guy that people expect a lot out of. We don’t accept that. He knows that.”
It’s not uncommon for Contreras to pick his moments to run hard, and the Brewers generally don’t mind that he does. He’s played at least 141 games and started at least 108 games behind the plate in each of his four seasons with the Brewers, and is the first catcher in Brewers history to catch at least 1,000 innings in three straight seasons. His 1,074 2/3 innings behind the plate this season are most in the Majors.
“There’s never going to be a time when you’re not responsible for playing winning baseball,” Murphy said. “It’s a guy that has done so much for the Brewers, he still has to abide by all the same [rules]. He doesn’t have to go 100 percent every time down the baseline, but when a guy muffs it, you have to be going hard enough that you’re safe if he does muff it.
“That’s winning baseball. Because that at-bat is important. Because every one of those at-bats is important.”
How did Murphy’s move land in the clubhouse?
“I think it’s great. I’m sure you guys have heard him say it because he says it to us all the time: ‘You can’t coast uphill,’” said first baseman Jake Bauers, who supplied Thursday night’s winning hit. “He wants [us] to keep [our] foot on the gas. We want to keep the foot on the gas. And we don’t want to go into the postseason feeling like we already did something. It’s really just, keep our heads down, keep working, keep preparing and go out and execute at a high clip.”
To be fair, Contreras was not the only player who raised Murphy’s ire. Yes, the Brewers won their 100th game in a season for the first time in club history. Yes, they completed a 7-2 final road trip in which they won every series and clinched the division, the best record in franchise history and a first-round bye in the postseason.
But a manager always sees ways his team can be better.
“Out of the 30 teams, very few over the next 10 years will win 100,” Murphy said. “I’m just grateful and proud to be a part of it, truly. And I’m proud we have this group of guys. Now, did we play great baseball tonight? No. Have we been playing great baseball? No. The strikeouts are concerning offensively.
“But, the guys, they like being together and they like this winning thing. They can’t take it for granted, because it’s special. But you have to put in the work to do it.”

item.content:encoded:
El beisbol mexicano sigue haciendo historia en las Grandes Ligas. Isaac Paredes y Jonathan Aranda se convirtieron en la primera pareja de jugadores nacidos en México que alcanza, en una misma temporada, al menos 20 cuadrangulares y 90 carreras impulsadas.
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Aroldis Chapman, el cubano que sigue haciendo historia en MLB!
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Braves regresan a la cima! Atlanta asegura el Este de la Nacional
Suscríbete al Newsletter de Unanimo y recibe gratis las últimas noticias. Dale click aquí
La hazaña llega en la recta final de la campaña 2026 y tiene como protagonistas a dos peloteros que conocen bien lo que significa representar a México en MLB. Paredes, nacido en Hermosillo, Sonora, juega actualmente con los Houston Astros, mientras que Aranda, originario de Tijuana, Baja California, milita con los Tampa Bay Rays.
Paredes llega a los últimos encuentros de la temporada con 23 jonrones y 92 carreras producidas, mientras Aranda acumula 22 cuadrangulares y 92 RBI. Es decir, ambos ya superaron ampliamente la barrera de las 90 impulsadas y se mantienen prácticamente igualados en producción ofensiva.
El logro adquiere todavía mayor relevancia al ponerlo en perspectiva histórica. Antes de 2026, los únicos jugadores nacidos en México que habían conseguido una temporada con al menos 20 jonrones y 90 carreras impulsadas eran Vinny Castilla e Isaac Paredes. Castilla alcanzó esa combinación en siete temporadas, mientras que Paredes lo había conseguido por primera vez en 2023.
Ahora Aranda se suma a ese grupo después de una campaña en la que se ha consolidado como uno de los principales bates mexicanos de las Grandes Ligas. Sus 22 jonrones también lo colocan entre los peloteros nacidos en México que han alcanzado al menos 20 vuelacercas en una temporada.
Pero la historia entre ambos no termina ahí. Aranda tiene un nuevo objetivo al alcance: el récord de 98 carreras impulsadas establecido por Paredes en 2023 durante su etapa con Tampa Bay. Con 92 RBI, el jugador de los Rays necesita seis más para igualar aquella marca y siete para establecer un nuevo récord.
Paredes, por su parte, también está escribiendo una temporada importante. Sus 23 jonrones representan su cuarta campaña con al menos 20 cuadrangulares en MLB, después de haber alcanzado esa cifra en 2022, 2023 y 2025. En 2023, además, tuvo su mejor producción de poder hasta ahora con 31 cuadrangulares y 98 carreras impulsadas.
La historia tiene un ingrediente especial porque Paredes y Aranda fueron compañeros en Tampa Bay entre 2022 y 2024. Durante esas tres temporadas compartieron vestidor antes de que Paredes fuera enviado a Houston, mientras Aranda permaneció con los Rays y asumió un papel cada vez más importante dentro de la ofensiva.
Ahora, los dos mexicanos compiten desde equipos diferentes, pero sus números cuentan una historia conjunta para el beisbol de México. Paredes ocupa actualmente uno de los primeros lugares históricos entre los mexicanos en jonrones y carreras producidas, mientras Aranda continúa escalando posiciones después de apenas cuatro temporadas en las Mayores.
Con la temporada regular entrando en sus últimos días, todavía queda por definir hasta dónde pueden llevar sus números. Paredes busca cerrar otra campaña de poder con Houston, mientras Aranda tiene una meta adicional: alcanzar las 98 carreras impulsadas de su antiguo compañero de equipo y convertirse en el nuevo referente mexicano en este departamento.
Lo que ya quedó registrado es que 2026 pertenece a ambos en la historia del beisbol mexicano. Por primera vez, dos jugadores nacidos en México alcanzaron simultáneamente la combinación de 20 jonrones y 90 carreras impulsadas en una misma temporada de Grandes Ligas.

item.content:encoded:
William Contreras News: Lifted due to lack of hustle
Brewers manager Pat Murphy said after Thursday's 5-1 win over the Phillies that he removed Contreras for a pinch hitter late because the backstop didn't run out a grounder he could have gotten a hit on, Curt Hogg of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reports.
This doesn't figure to have any real implications for Contreras' playing time moving forward, but it sends a message to the clubhouse that a lack of hustle will not be tolerated. Contreras was an All-Star this season -- his third career All-Star selection -- and he has been hot for Milwaukee with an .886 OPS in September entering Thursday's game.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Juan Soto blames self for Mets missing playoffs in 2026; hopes team is active this offseason
item.dc:creator: Phillip Martinez
item.description: The 2026 season was nothing like Juan Soto envisioned for himself or the Mets, and he put a lot of the team's woes this year on himself. item.content:encoded:
The 2026 season was nothing like Juan Soto envisioned for himself or the Mets, and he put a lot of the team's woes this year on himself.
Speaking with Mike Puma of the NY Post prior to the Mets' 3-1 loss to the Rangers on Thursday, the slugger said he needed to play better to get the team where they need to be.
"It's definitely not what I imagined in my head," Soto said. "There is nothing I can do other than blame myself. I have got to be better. I have got to be at the level to take us forward."
The slugger boasts formidable numbers despite playing in just 108 games (with three still left to play), but two stints on the IL due to separate calf injuries played a part in the Mets missing out on the playoffs for the second consecutive season.
Following Thursday's game, Soto is slashing .274/.393/.522 with an OPS of .915 to go along with his 27 home runs and 68 RBI.
But Soto missed a couple of weeks in April for his first calf injury, and then a month for the second in July/August. By the time he returned, the Mets sold at the trade deadline and the team was on the verge of being eliminated from playoff contention.
Despite missing the postseason, Soto told The Post he likes the direction the Mets are headed, especially with its young core of Carson Benge, Nolan McLean, A.J. Ewing and more.
"We have a young core, and we have got to maintain that young core and encourage them to the right way, the right path for the future," Soto said. "I think we are going in the right direction.
"Look at the young core and what they have been doing their first year in the big leagues. I think it's real special. It's always the first and second years are probably the toughest ones of your career, so what they're doing, I think is very special."
But with expectations being high in 2027, Soto hopes the organization is active this offseason to add to the core of veterans that includes him and Francisco Lindor -- and potentially Bo Bichette if he opts in -- and the aforementioned young core so that Soto sees playoff baseball for the first time as a member of the New York Mets.
When Soto was asked about Tarik Skubal, a pending free agent and a fellow Scott Boras client, as a potential addition, the perennial All-Star said he wants to see the Mets bring in anyone who can help the team.
"We should go and get as much as we can," Soto said. "We need as much help as we can get. It was a real tough year for us, so I think we have got to go out there and grab as much as we can."

item.title: [Seattle Sports] Cal Raleigh: Seattle Mariners' season a 'collective failure' - Seattle Sports
item.dc:creator: Zac Hereth
item.description: Cal Raleigh addresses the Mariners’ ‘collective failure’ this season The star catcher spoke candidly after Seattle was eliminated from playoff contention. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images) The Seattle Mariners have had some disappointing seasons over their 50-year history, but none may reach the levels of frustration that were produced by what transpired on the field this year. The club was a popular pick to represent the American League in the World Series after falling just one game shy of accompl
item.content:encoded:
Cal Raleigh addresses the Mariners’ ‘collective failure’ this season
The star catcher spoke candidly after Seattle was eliminated from playoff contention.
(Steph Chambers/Getty Images)
The Seattle Mariners have had some disappointing seasons over their 50-year history, but none may reach the levels of frustration that were produced by what transpired on the field this year.
The club was a popular pick to represent the American League in the World Series after falling just one game shy of accomplishing the feat the year prior. And with the AL West looking as feeble as ever, just about any analyst around the game believed Seattle would win its second straight division title.
The Mariners themselves embraced the high expectations and made it clear they had their sights set on the World Series.
But with four games remaining in the season Thursday, the club saw it’s playoff hopes unceremoniously dashed as it could do nothing but watch while the Texas Rangers beat the New York Mets 3-1 in a game that finished roughly 4 1/2 hours before the M’s took the field for their series opener against the Los Angeles Angels.
With the fate of their season officially sealed, catcher Cal Raleigh addressed what led to his team’s underwhelming year.
“I think we could point to a lot of things that went wrong, but I don’t think it was one thing, I don’t I think it was one person, I don’t think it was one department that failed this year,” Raleigh told reporters in the Mariners’ dugout Thursday at T-Mobile Park. “I think it was a collective failure, unfortunately. It’s going to take a lot of people having some self-reflection – myself included – on the direction of where we’re heading, what we want to be and who we want to be as a team.”
Raleigh believes this year’s Mariners lacked an identity and failed to seek out the edges needed to win games during the grueling schedule that is the 162-game baseball season, even using the “chasing edges” mantra Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald is known for.
“I don’t feel like there was (an identity) this year,” Raleigh said. “That is partly on me as a leader of this team. It’s not all on me, but as somebody who’s been here, it’s important for us to kind of come together and figure that out… We just never really got there with it. You can’t rely on starting pitching to carry you. You can’t rely on the bullpen. You can’t rely on the big home run every single time. You have to be able to win in different fashions, win in different ways, find a way to sneak out those one-run ballgames.”
Raleigh pointed to many areas Seattle struggled in this year – defense, playing on the road, hitting with runners in scoring position, record in one-run games – as reasons why this year went in the direction did. He called out the club for “a lack of focus, a lack of execution (and) a lack of energy.”
“It’s disappointing. We definitely didn’t deserve to make the playoffs. Just a frustrating year in general,” he said.
There was also perhaps too much faith in their own talent that the season would eventually turn itself around.
“I think it’s staff, I think it’s front office, I think it’s players, I think it’s from top to bottom – we could have been a little more aggressive,” Raleigh said. “… We’re grown men here, we’re trying to get to the same the same goal. And if it hurts somebody’s feelings, it hurt somebody’s feelings for a day, but at least that got taken care of… That’s something that’s that will be addressed and be better.”
The word “accountability” came up several times as Raleigh answered questions. He said this offseason should give players time to reflect on what went wrong and start to figure out what needs to be done to avoid the same sort of disappointment in 2027.
“If it happens once, it’s one too many times. And if it happens again, it becomes a habit,” Raleigh said. “So, it’s just about changing that and making sure you turn it around.”
As for the uncharacteristic struggles from Seattle’s pitching staff, Raleigh highlighted early injuries to the bullpen (Matt Brash and Cooper Criswell landed on the IL on consecutive days in June) as a contributing factor, but said the team needs more depth and more pitchers who can get swing and miss in that area. He also noticed how teams were attacking the club’s strike-throwing starting rotation.
“I saw a lot of very aggressive hitters and guys that were ready to go from pitch one because that’s kind of been our DNA,” Raleigh said. “We got to continue to get better and continue finding ways to combat that. I think we’ve done a great job with that and creating pitchers and having guys that are really good at (throwing strikes). But at the end of day, it’s about execution. It’s not about chasing a stat or doing anything like that. It’s just about getting better.”
Raleigh still believes in the core of this Mariners team, but feels it ultimately needs to get better from within.
“It’s not always bring in extra pieces that are going to help. Do we need to bring in more people in certain areas of the game? Yes, 100%. We need to get better and that’s always going to help,” Raleigh said, “but at the same time, when you look at the core guys, I think you could look at most of the guys and they would tell you that they did not have the season they wanted and team-wise did not have the season we wanted.”

MLB 애틀랜타, 신시내티에 6-7 역전패…침묵 길어진 김하성은 결장
[시카고=AP/뉴시스] 애틀랜타 브레이브스의 김하성이 17일(한국 시간) 미국 일리노이주 시카고의 리글리 필드에서 열린 2026 메이저리그(MLB) 시카고 컵스와의 원정 경기에서 5회초 내야 뜬공을 치고 있다. 2026.09.17
[서울=뉴시스]문채현 기자 = 메이저리그(MLB) 애틀랜타 브레이브스가 아쉬운 역전패를 당했다. 시즌 막판 다시 침묵이 길어진 김하성(애틀랜타)은 그라운드를 밟지 못했다.
애틀랜타는 25일(한국 시간) 미국 조지아주 애틀랜타의 트루이스트파크에서 열린 2026 MLB 신시내티 레즈와의 홈 경기에서 6-7로 패했다.
전날(24일) 연장 접전 끝에 10회 끝내기 승리를 거뒀던 애틀랜타는 기세를 잇지 못했다.
최근 3경기 연속 선발 출장 기회를 얻고도 무안타에 그쳤던 김하성은 이날 벤치에 앉았다.
김하성은 지난 12일 필라델피아 필리스전 이후 2주 가까이 안타를 추가하지 못했다.
김하성은 올 시즌 49경기에 나서 타율 0.113(124타수 14안타) 9타점 8득점의 성적을 기록 중이다.
0-1로 밀린 채 1회말에 들어간 애틀랜타는 무사 1, 3루에 맷 올슨의 희생플라이로 빠르게 동점을 만들었고, 이어 마이클 해리스 2세, 마우리시오 듀본, 오지 알비스의 연속 안타로 3-1 역전에 성공했다. 이어진 1사 만루엔 오스틴 라일리의 희생플라이로 4-1까지 달아났다.
하지만 리드는 오래가지 않았다.
애틀랜타는 2회 1점을 실점한 뒤 3회초 엘리 데 라 크루즈에게 시즌 30호포를 내주며 1점 차 추격을 받았다.
이어진 2사 2, 3루엔 에우제니오 수아레즈에게 적시타를 헌납하며 4-5 역전을 허용했다.
애틀랜타는 3회말 라일리의 솔로포, 5회말 2사 2루에 마이크 야스트렘스키의 적시타로 재역전에 성공했으나, 신시내티는 6회초 엑토르 로드리게스의 투런포로 다시 리드를 가져갔다.
애틀랜타는 경기 막판까지 추가 득점을 내지 못하고 6-7로 패했다.
이미 지구 1위를 확정한 애틀랜타는 시즌 66패(93승)째를 당했다.

item.title: [reviewingthebrew.com] Brewers reach 100 wins for first time in franchise history thanks to key roster strength
item.dc:creator: Owen Jonas
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers have a 100-win season. item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers have a 100-win season. With a victory over the Philadelphia Phillies on Thursday night, the 2026 Brew Crew improved to 100-59 on the 2026 season, reaching an unbelievable milestone that hadn't been accomplished in the first 57 seasons of the franchise's history.
After projection models expected the Brewers to finish with somewhere between 80-85 wins during the 2026 season, Pat Murphy's squad has proved the preseason predictions wrong once again. However, they didn't just surpass their expected win total by a few games; they blew past the projections, produced the best regular season in franchise history, and reached the elusive 100-win mark.
It's an unbelievable accomplishment, one that is made even more impressive by the fact that Milwaukee has produced 90+ win seasons in each of the last four seasons and five times in the last six years. This isn't a one-off season in which the Brewers sacrificed their future and went "all in" on one year. Rather, it's just another chapter in what has easily been the most successful stretch of seasons in franchise history. Put another way, to win 100 games with the best farm system in baseball makes the achievement that much more incredible.
It took a pair of wins over the Philadelphia Phillies, who still have plenty to play for, to achieve 100 wins before their final series of the regular season. With the Brewers fully in postseason preparation mode, made clear by a number of roster and in-game decisions, Murphy's team displayed their impressive depth in their late-September series victory over the Phillies. Said roster depth will be key in the postseason.
Brewers' rely on impressive roster depth to reach elusive 100-win mark after postseason preparation has begun
The Brewers entered Thursday night's series finale against the Phillies with a first-round bye, and therefore a spot in the NLDS, already secured. They didn't have nearly as much to play for as Philadelphia, who is fighting to secure home-field advantage in the Wild Card Series. As a result, Murphy turned to Shane Drohan, who is expected to be a reliever in October, for a short start, didn't include Christian Yelich or Jackson Chourio in the starting lineup, and opted to have William Contreras DH during the series finale on Thursday night. Murphy didn't use Abner Uribe or Trevor Megill and kept Antonio Senzatela in for a save in the ninth inning, and yet, even with their postseason preparation fully underway, the Brewers knocked off the mighty Phillies, who have not officially clinched a spot in the postseason just yet.
In other words, the Brewers won their 100th game of the season on Thursday night due to their impressive roster depth. Murphy's squad proved that they can defeat a postseason team like the Phillies without using one of their top starters, without starting Chourio or Yelich, and without turning to their elite high-leverage duo at the end of the ballgame.
That type of roster depth bodes well for Milwaukee's chances in October. A deep postseason run, like the one the Brewers are hoping to put together, requires contributions throughout the roster. Whether it be a pinch-hit appearance, escaping a jam in the middle innings, or serving as a defensive replacement late in the game, the 26 Brewers that Milwaukee elects to include on their postseason roster will each have their role. It's therefore encouraging to see so many of them contribute to the Brewers' late-season series win over the Phillies, which led to 100 wins.
The Brewers have three games left to improve their record-breaking regular season record even further. Expect a similar strategy, in which Murphy relies on his depth to give necessary rest to each of his players, in the Brewers' upcoming weekend series against the St. Louis Cardinals. That said, regardless of how the final series plays out, the 2026 Brewers officially have a 100-win season to their name -- a truly incredible accomplishment.

item.content:encoded:
Brewers take down Phillies for franchise's first 100-win season
(Photo credit: Bill Streicher)
Jake Bauers' RBI single in the eighth inning plated the go-ahead run Thursday for the Milwaukee Brewers, who reached the 100-win mark for the first time in franchise history with their 5-1 win over the hosting Philadelphia Phillies.
Bauers, who went 2-for-5 and added a double, singled up the middle, allowing Jackson Chourio to score from second, giving the Brewers (100-59) a 2-1 lead and starting a three-run frame. Chourio, who pinch-hit for designated hitter William Contreras, led off the frame with a walk off Jose Alvarado (5-4) and stole second.
Gary Sanchez singled deep to left field to put runners on the corners, and after Alvarado got Luis Lara to line out to shallow center, Cooper Pratt (2-for-3) welcomed Chase Shugart with another hit up the middle to give the Brewers a two-run lead. Joey Ortiz added a two-out hit, a blooper to shallow center that allowed Sanchez to score from second.
Chourio added a solo home run, his 25th blast of the season, in the ninth.
Five Brewers pitchers held the Phillies (87-72) to just four hits. JoJo Romero (3-3) allowed one hit in 1 1/3 innings against St. Louis, who Milwaukee acquired him from last month. Romero picked up his second win with the Brewers since coming off the injured list (appendectomy) earlier this month.
Antonio Senzatela relieved Romero, allowing a walk over the final 1 2/3 innings to earn his fourth save.
Phillies starter Andrew Painter held the Brewers to just one run over six innings. The rookie allowed five hits and three walks while matching a season-high eight strikeouts. His only blemish came in the second, when Sal Frelick doubled home Sanchez.
Kyle Schwarber (2-for-4) and Bryce Harper (2-for-4) combined to get all four of the Phillies hits. Harper's third-inning single scored Schwarber, who led off the frame with a double off Brewers starter Shane Drohan. Philadelphia managed just one hit, a Schwarber single in the seventh, against the Brewers bullpen.
Besides losing the game, the Phillies may also have lost infielder Luis Arraez, who reportedly sprained an ankle trying to avoid a tag on a groundout in the sixth inning.
With the win, Milwaukee can officially clinch home-field advantage throughout the postseason should the Los Angeles Dodgers lose Thursday night to the visiting San Diego Padres.
Philadelphia remains in an NL wild-card spot, but the Phillies could not drop their magic number to clinch from two.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Alex Bregman's wild MLB playoff streak has star in rare air – injured face willing
Major League Baseball’s playoffs are coming soon and Alex Bregman will be a part of it.
Of course he is.
Bregman made baseball history Thursday, Sept. 24 when the Chicago Cubs clinched a National League wild-card berth with a victory over the Miami Marlins. And for the 10th consecutive year, injured eye willing, Bregman will take part in the postseason, this time with a twist.
Bregman, the Cubs’ 32-year-old third baseman, will become the first position player to play postseason baseball 10 consecutive seasons with multiple teams. In fact, he’s done it with three ballclubs – eight straight years with the Houston Astros and then the past two with the Boston Red Sox and Cubs, as he settled for good in Chicago by signing a five-year, $175 million contract in January.
And it seems like wherever Bregman goes, October baseball follows.
Texas loves him anyway
Bregman was a two-time All-Star and two-time champion in Houston, the brash young slugger in his first full season when they won the 2017 World Series, the MVP runner-up when they lost the 2019 Series in seven games.
After bearing much of the scorn for the club’s 2017 sign-stealing scandal, he was the chastened veteran on the 2022 squad that won a second World Series, this time without a cloud of controversy to follow.
Yet Bregman’s chops as a club cornerstone gained greater veracity a year ago, when he left the Astros and, combining his production with his baseball smarts and clubhouse gravitas, lifted the Red Sox to the postseason for the first time in three years as the Astros missed the playoffs for the first time since 2016.
Those vibes were as attractive to the Cubs as Bregman’s career .846 OPS when they pursued him after he opted out of his contract with Boston. And it’s all come together in Wrigleyville: Thanks to a second-half surge, Bregman has hit 26 home runs, posted an .804 OPS and produced 5.4 WAR, second only to presumed MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong on the Cubs.
“Anytime Alex Bregman is playing an Alex Bregman brand of baseball, it’s just good for the program,” Crow-Armstrong told USA TODAY Sports last month.
And if he manages to play just days after suffering a gruesome eye injury, the legend will only grow.
Heroes of the fall
Bregman’s postseason constancy has put himself among some legendary and curious October stalwarts.
Unsurprisingly, the consecutive postseasons list is littered with alumni from the three dominant playoff groups of the wild-card era: The 1990s Atlanta Braves, the late-century New York Yankees and the current batch of Los Angeles Dodgers.
Yankees closer Mariano Rivera tops the list, appearing in 13 consecutive postseasons from 1995-2007, followed by Derek Jeter, whose 12-year streak began a year after Rivera’s playoff debut.
Catcher Jorge Posada and Braves Hall of Famers Chipper Jones and Tom Glavine all played in 11 consecutive postseasons. As did lefty reliever Mike Stanton, who did it with four teams – the Braves, Red Sox, Yankees and Texas Rangers – between 1991-2002.
Who let him in?
Bregman, longtime Dodgers closer Kenley Jansen and Hall of Famer Greg Maddux all reached 10 consecutive postseasons. Current Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman and longtime third baseman Justin Turner are at the nine-year mark, Freddie winning a World Series championship with Atlanta in 2021 and two more in L.A. the past two seasons.
Retired Dodgers lefty Clayton Kershaw leads the “but for” category: He pitched in eight consecutive postseasons from 2013-2020, and would have made it 13 in a row if not for injuries in 2021 and 2024. Same with Braves Hall of Famer John Smoltz – he was present for all of Atlanta’s 14 consecutive division titles yet underwent Tommy John surgery in 2000.
And several likely 2026 participants had streaks broken thanks to one unlucky season – such as slugger Kyle Schwarber, who’d be working on a 12-year streak with the Cubs, Red Sox and Phillies if not for the 2019 Cubs missing the playoffs. Same with Mookie Betts, ticketed for his 10th postseason in 11 years with the Dodgers and Boston, missing only in ’19 with the Red Sox.
The wild-card format – which began in 1995 and expanded in 2012 and 2022 – makes this list unavoidably modern due to the expanded access it affords. Still, some players from past eras were near-constants in the playoffs.
Mr. October himself, Reggie Jackson, reached the postseason 10 times in 12 years from 1971 to 1982, winning four World Series with the Oakland Athletics and New York Yankees, and then, just for kicks, reaching the 1982 ALCS with the California Angels.
The great Yogi Berra was a 10-time World Series champion, but his longest consecutive streak of playoff runs was five years. Yet reaching the World Series 14 times in 17 years, when only two teams reached the playoffs, remains a stunning feat.
So perhaps Bregman - even with 102 career postseason games, 19 homers, 91 hits and a .791 OPS - has a little more work to do to match some of the legends of October. Yet from Houston to Boston to Chicago, he’s leaving little doubt that wherever he goes, winning follows.

item.title: [wtae.com] Pirates win final home game, clinch first non-losing season since 2018
item.dc:creator: WILL GRAVES AP Sports Writer
item.description: Pirates beat the Cardinals 2-1 to secure their first non-losing season since 2018 Ronny Simon raced home on Spencer Horwitz's eighth inning sacrifice fly and the Pittsburgh Pirates assured themselves of the club's first non-losing season in eight years with a 2-1 win over the St. Louis Cardinals on Thursday. item.content:encoded:
Pirates beat the Cardinals 2-1 to secure their first non-losing season since 2018
Ronny Simon raced home on Spencer Horwitz's eighth inning sacrifice fly and the Pittsburgh Pirates assured themselves of the club's first non-losing season in eight years with a 2-1 win over the St. Louis Cardinals on Thursday.
Simon reached on a walk by Ryne Stanek (2-3), advanced to second on a wild pitch and scooted to third when the throw from catcher Ivan Herrera skipped into center field for an error. Horwitz's flyball to center was plenty deep enough for Simon to score.
Luke Weaver (4-1) got the final out of the eighth for Pittsburgh. Mason Montgomery struck out the side in the ninth for his 17th save in 19 chances as Pittsburgh improved to 81-78 with three games to go. The club's previous non-losing season came in 2018 when it won 82 games.
Reigning NL Cy Young Award winner Paul Skenes ended an uneven year by his standards with 6 1/3 excellent innings in his 32nd and final start.
The 24-year-old, whose performance this year has been met with mild criticism locally, allowed one run, three hits and two walks and six strikeouts. He received a loud ovation when he was removed by manager Don Kelly after recording his 200th strikeout of the season when Cardinals designated hitter Leo Bernal was caught looking leading off the seventh.
Skenes became just the second pitcher in the franchise's 145-year history to reach 200 strikeouts in consecutive seasons. He finished 10-11 with a 3.82 ERA, nearly double the MLB-leading 1.97 ERA he posted in 2025.
St. Louis fell to 77-82, assured of consecutive losing seasons for the first time since the shortened 1994 and 1995 seasons.
Alec Burleson hit his 24th homer of the season in the first inning for the Cardinals.
Up next
The Cardinals wrap up the season with a three-game set at NL Central champion Milwaukee while Pittsburgh heads to Detroit to face the Tigers.

El segunda base de los Filis de Filadelfia, Luis Arráez, tuvo que ser ayudado a salir del campo tras sufrir una lesión en el tobillo mientras corría hacia la primera base tras conectar un batazo por el cuadro durante el juego del jueves contra los Cerveceros de Milwaukee.
Los Filis informaron posteriormente que Arráez sufrió un esguince en el tobillo izquierdo y que será sometido a evaluaciones adicionales, según Todd Zolecki de MLB.com.
Acción durante el juego
Arráez intentó evitar el toque del inicialista de los Cerveceros, Jake Bauers, y se dobló la pierna al estirarse para pisar la almohadilla.
- Inmediatamente cayó al suelo con dolor mientras se sujetaba la pierna izquierda.

item.content:encoded:
Chris Sale, de Atlanta, se mete a un club histórico con 200 ponches
El zurdo alcanzó la marca por novena ocasión en su carrera; a los 37 años, el estelar de los Bravos cerró una temporada espectacular y ahora apunta a octubre
Chris Sale volvió a hacer historia. El zurdo de los Atlanta Braves alcanzó los 200 ponches en una temporada por novena ocasión en su carrera, una cifra que lo coloca junto a algunos de los nombres más importantes en la historia del pitcheo de las Grandes Ligas.
La marca llegó este miércoles 23 de septiembre, durante el triunfo de Atlanta por 3-2 sobre los Cincinnati Reds, en un encuentro que terminó en extrainnings. Sale ponchó a 10 bateadores en 5.2 entradas y consiguió el abanicado número 200 al retirar a Sal Stewart en la sexta entrada.
El detalle no es menor. Con esta actuación, Sale se convirtió en el lanzador con más temporadas de 200 ponches desde 2013, además de convertirse en apenas el segundo pitcher zurdo en la historia de MLB con nueve campañas de al menos 200 ponches, solamente detrás de Randy Johnson, quien lo hizo en 13 ocasiones.
UNA LISTA CON PUROS MONSTRUOS DEL MONTÍCULO
La lista histórica de temporadas con 200 o más ponches tiene a Nolan Ryan al frente con 15, seguido por Randy Johnson con 13, Roger Clemens con 12 y Tom Seaver con 10. Ahora Sale aparece inmediatamente detrás de ellos con nueve campañas.
Lo curioso es que Sale consiguió semejante cifra a los 37 años, cuando muchos lanzadores veteranos ya han reducido considerablemente su velocidad y capacidad para generar swings fallidos. El zurdo, en cambio, cerró la campaña regular con 200 ponches en 162.2 entradas, además de una efectividad de 2.16, 14 victorias y 9 derrotas.
Y todavía hay más. En su última apertura de la temporada, Sale volvió a mostrar que su brazo está lejos de pedir vacaciones. De sus 97 lanzamientos ante Cincinnati, 12 alcanzaron al menos las 99 millas por hora, mientras que Statcast registró una velocidad máxima de 99.9 mph.
La velocidad ha sido una de las historias más llamativas de Sale durante 2026. MLB ya había documentado que el zurdo estaba lanzando más fuerte que en buena parte de sus últimas temporadas, incluso llegando a 99.6 mph con su recta de cuatro costuras en una actuación contra los Dodgers.
Su temporada también tuvo otra actuación espectacular contra Los Ángeles: el 27 de agosto lanzó una blanqueada completa de nueve entradas, ponchó a 11 bateadores y permitió solamente dos imparables, una muestra del nivel que mantuvo durante la segunda mitad del calendario.
El resultado final fue una campaña en la que Sale terminó con 2.16 de efectividad, 200 ponches y un WHIP de 0.98, números que lo mantuvieron entre los brazos más dominantes de la Liga Nacional.
El logro de Sale llegó justo cuando Atlanta ya había asegurado su boleto a la postemporada y, posteriormente, conquistó el título de la División Este de la Liga Nacional, el séptimo de la franquicia en las últimas nueve temporadas.
Ahora viene la parte verdaderamente importante. Sale está proyectado para abrir el Juego 1 de la Serie de Comodines de la Liga Nacional, si Atlanta mantiene el tercer puesto de la siembra. La Serie de Comodines comenzará el 29 de septiembre y se disputará a tres juegos.
El escenario todavía puede cambiar porque Atlanta busca mejorar su posición en la tabla, pero el plan del cuerpo técnico ya está definido alrededor de su principal carta. Chris Sale será el encargado de ponerle la pelota al guante cuando los Bravos arranquen su camino hacia octubre.
UNA CARRERA QUE SIGUE AGREGANDO CAPÍTULOS
El nuevo registro se suma a una colección de números que ya hacen de Sale uno de los lanzadores más destacados de su generación. En 2025 se convirtió en el pitcher que más rápido alcanzó los 2,500 ponches en la historia de MLB, al conseguirlo en apenas 2,026 entradas, superando la marca que pertenecía precisamente a Randy Johnson.
Además, Sale ya posee un Premio Cy Young de la Liga Nacional, ganado en 2024, y múltiples selecciones al Juego de Estrellas. Su trayectoria también incluye pasos por White Sox y Red Sox antes de convertirse en una pieza fundamental de Atlanta.
Ahora, a los 37 años, el zurdo tiene otro número redondo en la vitrina: nueve temporadas con 200 ponches. Y mientras los libros de historia comienzan a hacerle espacio, Sale tiene una preocupación mucho más inmediata.
Octubre está a la vuelta de la esquina y el brazo izquierdo de los Bravos todavía tiene bastante veneno.

item.content:encoded:
El pitcher tabasqueño Jesús Broca es subcampeón de la Southern League en Ligas Menores
El orgullo de la ranchería Boquerón firmó un extraordinario verano con la sucursal de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee
El lanzador tabasqueño Jesús Broca se proclamó subcampeón con Biloxi Shuckers en la Southern League de Clase Doble “A” en las Ligas Menores.
El orgullo de la ranchería Boquerón firmó un extraordinario verano con la sucursal de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee, aunque se quedó con el segundo lugar, tras caer 3-1 en el juego 3 ante Rocket City Trash Pandas.
Biloxi Shuckers perdió 2-1 en la serie, pero en el tercer duelo vendió cara la derrota, en un juego donde ambas novenas demostraron su poder con el madero al conectar 10 imparables cada una.
En ese tercer partido, el serpentinero del edén mexicano entró a relevar a JD. Thompson en el cuarto episodio, para lanzar en una entrada completa, permitiendo un hit, recetando dos ponches que dejaron en cero su porcentaje de efectividad.
Con esto, termina una campaña formidable del pitcher choco, que en la temporada regular culminó con marca de 3-6 en ganados y perdidos en 58.1 entradas lanzadas.
Además, la gran temporada que tuvo Jesús Broca lo hizo colocarse entre los 10 mejores prospectos mexicanos de Grandes Ligas por el prestigiado portal Baseball América.

item.content:encoded:
PHILADELPHIA — Philadelphia Phillies second baseman Luis Arraez left Thursday's game against Milwaukee with a sprained left ankle after he tried to avoid a tag at first base.
Arraez is a three-time batting champion and entered the game batting .311 to lead to the National League.
Arraez hit a grounder to shortstop Cooper Pratt, and a wide throw pulled first baseman Jake Bauers off the bag.
Arraez dived to his right to avoid the tag and immediately grabbed his ankle. Arraez, obtained from San Francisco at the trade deadline, stayed down for a while as trainers tended to him. He eventually hobbled off the field with assistance.
He left with the game tied 1-1 in the sixth inning. The Phillies needed to beat the Brewers and have the San Diego Padres lose to the Los Angeles Dodgers later in the night to clinch their fifth straight playoff appearance.
Bryson Stott moved from third base to second and Edmundo Sosa took over at third.

Arraez’s injury couldn’t have come at a worse time, as the Phillies will likely play in the NL Wild Card round next week.
The Phillies acquired Arraez from the San Francisco Giants before the trade deadline.
GettyWASHINGTON, DC – SEPTEMBER 15: Luis Arraez #4 of the Philadelphia Phillies doubles during the eighth inning against the Washington Nationals at Nationals Park on September 15, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images)
Since joining the Phillies, Arraez, 29, has slashed .278/.309/.369 with two home runs and 21 RBI over 46 games.
He hit .324/.360/.440 with four home runs and 43 RBI over 105 games with the Giants this season.
GettyPHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – SEPTEMBER 5: Luis Arraez #4 of the Philadelphia Phillies reacts after hitting an RBI single in the bottom of the first inning against the Atlanta Braves at Citizens Bank Park on September 5, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images)
Arraez will be a free agent at the end of the season. He signed a one-year deal with San Francisco over the offseason.
The second baseman has eight years of big-league experience. He has played for the Minnesota Twins, Miami Marlins, San Diego Padres, Giants and Phillies.
Arraez has a career slash line of .316/.361/.415 with 42 home runs and 372 RBI.
Philadelphia Phillies Right Now

The Phillies are the last NL Wild Card team with an 87-71 record.
They are a half-game behind the Chicago Cubs for the second Wild Card spot and one game back of the San Diego Padres for the top Wild Card spot.
GettyPHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – SEPTEMBER 22: Jhoan Duran #59 and Derek Hill #49 of the Philadelphia Phillies celebrate after the win against the Milwaukee Brewers at Citizens Bank Park on September 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images)
The Arizona Diamondbacks are 2 1/2 games behind the Phillies for the final Wild Card spot.
Philadelphia will finish the regular season with a three-game series against the Tampa Bay Rays at Citizens Bank Park this weekend.

item.title: [purplerow.com] Rockies bid farewell to Coors Field with 12-8 loss to the Diamondbacks
item.dc:creator: Skyler Timmins
item.description: What began as a blowout deficit ended in a close loss as the Colorado Rockies’ last chance at some “LoDo Magic” fell short in a 12-8 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks. The Rockies suffered the sweep while finishing 32-49 at Coors Field this season. item.content:encoded:
What began as a blowout deficit ended in a close loss as the Colorado Rockies’ last chance at some “LoDo Magic” fell short in a 12-8 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks. The Rockies suffered the sweep while finishing 32-49 at Coors Field this season.
Attack of the Snakes
The first inning has been a disaster for the Rockies most of the season, but especially during their slide over the last few weeks. There was hope with Tanner Gordon on the mound, who has had strong numbers in the first inning and could buck the trend and start the team off with a solid chance in the final home game.
The Diamondbacks had other intentions.
Lars Nootbar started the game with a hot shot down the first-base line that TJ Rumfield managed to stop from going for extra bases. However, Gordon was late getting off the mound and it turned into an infield single. Gordon then walked Ketel Marte, followed by a three-run home run off the bat of Gabriel Moreno to make it 3-0.
Geraldo Perdomo then launched a ball to center field for a triple before coming in to score on a bloop single to left field by Pavin Smith for the fourth run of the inning. Nolan Arenado then followed with his 29th home run of the season, a two-run shot to make it 6-0.
Gordon finally escaped the inning, but six runs in the first brought the total number of runs allowed in the opening frame of the series to 13. The Rockies have also allowed a run in the first in 12 of their last 17 games.
The Diamondbacks kept the foot on the gas in the second inning as Nootbar singled to lead off and scored on Marte’s RBI double. Perdomo later blooped a single into shallow center field to score another run, making it 8-0 after two innings.
After a scoreless third inning, Gordon’s day would come to an end early in the fourth inning. Perdomo led off the inning with a walk, the fourth of the game and a new career high for Gordon. Smith’s then delivered an RBI double. Gordon managed to strike out Arenado, but then surrendered a single to Corbin Carroll to end his afternoon, but was still tagged for the 10th Arizona run when James McCann singled to left field off reliever Jimmy Herget.
Gordon lasted just 3.1 innings, allowing 10 runs on 12 hits with four walks and just one strikeout. The Diamondbacks were not fooled by his fastball, meaning he had to rely on his secondary pitches, which he struggled to command. When he did have to throw a fastball, Arizona made sure to square up the ball and do damage. Despite pounding the zone as usual, Gordon threw 96 pitches and induced three groundouts and five flyouts, but only had three swings and misses.
The Bullpen Fire Brigade
Having to take on another heavy workload, the bullpen did an admirable job settling down the Diamondbacks offense.
Herget picked up 2.2 innings of work and was solid enough despite giving up an RBI single to Arenado in the fifth inning and a McCann home run in the sixth inning to make it 12-1. He still managed four strikeouts against one walk while surrendering four hits, but his 49 pitches helped navigate to the later frames.
Nick Frasso and Juan Mejia then followed with scoreless seventh and eighth innings, respectively, setting the tone after the Diamondbacks had started subbing out players. Jordan Romano then took over the ninth and, despite giving up a triple, fired a clean inning.
E-Rod Domination
While the Diamondback offense had a productive day at the plate against Gordon, the Rockies offense couldn’t quite figure out Eduardo Rodriguez. The veteran left-hander breezed his way through six innings, allowing just two runs on nine hits with three strikeouts. Utilizing four grounders and seven easy flyouts, Rodriguez threw 92 pitches and stayed in the zone consistently. He had a 63% first-pitch strike rate and 12 swings and misses. His changeup was particularly effective, generating a 21% whiff rate.
The Rockies scratched across their first run in the fourth inning against Rodriguez when Rumfield singled to lead off. Cole Carrigg and Kyle Karros both singled to then load the bases. Brett Sullivan then hit into a fielder’s choice that allowed the run to score, but put runners on the corners with one out. Unfortunately, the Rockies couldn’t scratch across any other runs. The next run wouldn’t come across until the sixth inning when Karros sent a belt-high fastball into left field for his 13th home run of the season, making it 12-2 Diamondbacks.
Here Come the Rockies!
Once Rodriguez was out of the game, the Rockies had begun a line change of their own in the seventh inning, but started to find some success against the Arizona bullpen.
Facing Dennis Santana, Zac Veen led off with a double down the line. Two batters later, Hunter Goodman delivered a one-out RBI single after a lengthy at-bat to make it 12-3.
Rumfield followed with a walk, setting the table for Carrigg to hit a three-run home run. It was his 11th of the season and got the Rockies back within six runs.
Taylor Clarke then took over the Diamondbacks in the eighth inning and ran into more trouble from the Rockies offense. Veen kicked off another rally with a towering home run to right field for his third of the season to make it 12-7.
Adael Amador then barrelled up a baseball to right for a double. After Goodman recorded the second out on a line drive, Rumfield lined a double to right to drive in another run and make it 12-8. With that double, Rumfield also tied Troy Tulowitzki for most times reaching safely in a rookie season at 243. Karros then threatened with a long fly ball that was caught shortly before the wall in left field to end the inning.
Unfortunately, the rally magic ran out as Kevin Ginkel worked a clean ninth inning to put the Rockies away. In the game, the Rockies had 17 hits, while striking out eight times against one walk. Carrigg led the way with four hits while four other hitters had two hits. They went 5-for-13 with runners in scoring position but left 10 on base.
Meanwhile, Arizona had 18 hits with seven strikeouts and five walks while going 6-for-15 with RISP. Oddly enough, they also left 10 men on base, but had three batters with three hits.
Up Next
The Rockies head off to the South Side of Chicago to take on the White Sox for the final three-game series of the season. Tomoyuki Sugano (菅野 智之) will face off against Sean Burke.
First pitch is at 5:40 pm MDT.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Juan Soto Joins Exclusive Club With Albert Pujols, 3 Hall of Famers
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
item.description: Juan Soto has been around the big leagues for long enough to almost forget just how young he is. Soto is in his ninth big league season, and yet he is somehow still just 27 years old. In comparison, New York Mets rookie starter Nolan McLean is 25 years old, and that's not a wild number, by any means. item.content:encoded:
Juan Soto has been around the big leagues for long enough to almost forget just how young he is.
Soto is in his ninth big league season, and yet he is somehow still just 27 years old. In comparison, New York Mets rookie starter Nolan McLean is 25 years old, and that's not a wild number, by any means. Soto is an anomaly, and it's why the Mets handed him a mammoth 15-year, $765 million deal ahead of the 2025 season.
With the Mets struggling throughout the season, Soto's greatness likely hasn't been talked about as much as it probably should. But this guy is special. One stat that jumps out is the fact that he's one of just five players in big league history with 250 or more homers and more walks than strikeouts before his 28th birthday, along with Albert Pujols, Mel Ott, Eddie Mathews and Jimmie Foxx, as shared on X by RotoBaller's Eric Cross.
Juan Soto Is Putting Himself Up There With The Greats
That's three Hall of Famers and Pujols, who will be in the second that he's eligible. If Soto can keep this up, he's well on his way as well.
On Thursday, Soto went 0-for-3 with a walk. For his career, Soto has 271 long balls and 972 walks, to just 897 strikeouts in 1,204 games played. He's not going to turn 28 years old until October 25. On the season, the young superstar is slashing .274/.393/.522 with 27 homers and 68 RBIs in 108 games played. The only thing that has slowed him down this season is injuries, and yet he has still had a good overall season. Over the last two seasons, he hit over 40 homers and drove in over 100 runs in at least 157 games. His numbers so far this season are on pace with his last few, if he didn't get hurt.
There are few guys in big league history who have been able to start a career like Soto has. He's a five-time All-Star, six-time Silver Slugger Award winner, one-time batting champ, one-time Home Run Derby champ and a World Series champion. And, again, he's just 27 years old. He should just get better.
He's already etched his name onto plenty of historic lists and the scary thing is the fact that realistically, we may not have seen his best yet. Theoretically, he should be just starting to enter his prime, and yet he's already historic.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick also received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding Fastball On SI, please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com

item.title: [motorcitybengals.com] 20 worst Detroit Tigers free agent signings in franchise history
item.dc:creator: Kurt Mensching
